titleEn: Is iPhone's Touch Really the Best
contentEn:
Everyone raves about the iPhone. The reasons cited are its flashy UI, touch capabilities, etc... But as a long-time smartphone user, I question if it's truly the best. Frankly, the flashy UI isn't something I particularly agree with, as Windows Mobile's default OS might not have offered it, but other applications had already implemented similar features. Among these points, let's talk briefly about touch.

**First, I feel that the fundamental goals of touch on the iPhone and Windows Mobile are different. This is because Windows Mobile has a stylus pen, and the iPhone does not. What I mean is... the iPhone aims for the finger as a natural interface.**

**1. Pen or Finger**
Naturally, this alone gives the iPhone an advantage. You don't forget the pen, nor do you need the hassle of taking it out... This is clearly where Jobs' philosophy shines. However, there are also things it sacrifices. Precise touch. Honestly, it's not possible. This is because fingers are inherently thick. Since a person's line of sight covers the LCD screen, pixel-level work is practically impossible. In fact, precise work itself might be pointless in such a small LCD mobile environment... but it's certain that precise work is impossible.

**2. The iPhone's touch is not precise.**
This disadvantage of being unable to perform precise work is particularly evident in handwriting recognition applications. [Writing characters using 2-3 cells at once](http://blog.naver.com/leojky/140059180088) is impossible on the iPhone. Of course, to overcome this drawback, the iPhone can sufficiently compensate with its large LCD and input via drawing across the entire screen. Windows Mobile also has such tools.

Perhaps Windows Mobile has an excessive level of precision that isn't necessary for a mobile environment. However, I wanted to point out that calling the iPhone's touch "precise" is not an appropriate description. And people like me tend to like such precision. That's because drawing with Windows Mobile is one of my hobbies.

The image below was drawn with [Pocket Artist 3.0](http://blog.naver.com/killkimno?Redirect=Log&logNo=70014024986) on Windows Mobile. (Most were drawn during bus commutes, taking less than 30 minutes each.)
The purpose is for [Me2day](http://me2day.net/fstory/). ^^;

Of course, compared to the old tablet I bought in '98, it's terrible. It's not even comparable to an Intuos. And even though the X1's LCD is a bit large... it's incredibly frustrating. This is also why I covet the HTC Touch HD2, and I simply desire a mobile platform device with a tablet that has pressure and tilt sensitivity.
(Am I too much of a maniac? ^^;) It's not a very common need, but I posted this to show that there are people like me who want precise pointing.

**3. Multi-touch**
- In this regard, Apple is a pioneer. I wasn't particularly impressed by anything else on the iPhone. It felt more like a compilation of existing good features. But this feature, I saw for the first time from Apple. [What's a bit annoying, however, is that they are trying to block other OSes as much as possible with patents](http://blog.naver.com/fstory97?Redirect=Log&logNo=70053493804). I understand that Apple did well and that it's good, but playing the game by excluding competitors like that seems unfair. This is because many of Apple's technologies were already used in existing WinMo devices, and as a user, I wish to see multi-touch platforms on various devices, not just one Apple model.
I heard that Windows 7 and Samsung had to put a lot of thought into implementing multi-touch while avoiding Apple's patents. Anyway, since it's supposed to come out later... we'll see then.

**4. But why does the iPhone's touch feel like the best? It's well-designed HCI**
My thoughts are as follows. In games, there's a sense of "shooting feel." When you fire a gun, and the feedback of sound, movement, and light are all in harmony, the feeling of shooting feels more realistic. However, the "real feeling" here is quite subjective. If you actually shoot a gun, it's just loud, and different from a game. HCI (Human-Computer Interface), often discussed in animation and UX, is a field that delves into subjective feelings rather than objective ones. It's in this area that Apple seems to be demonstrating outstanding performance.

**5. What truly creates the touch experience is a stable kernel and apps**
However, I don't see this as a strength of the OS. This is because I question whether the OS should really be responsible for such aspects. Fundamentally, the OS's faithfulness is to run applications safely, quickly, and well. (The problem is that Windows Mobile didn't even do well with this basic OS faithfulness. Windows 7 seems to be rebuilding the kernel from scratch, so it might improve.) And the method Apple used to maximize this assurance is closure and control. The problem with Windows Mobile was that too many free applications threatened the stability of the OS itself. While comparing it to Windows Mobile, which was built long ago on Windows CE, is unfair in itself, the variety of devices also contributes to degrading OS performance. In a mobile environment, even decimal-point-level stuttering makes users subtly feel that something is off.
Apple with its flashy UI. If we only talk about that, I think it's no different from Windows, which just added flashy UIs and sold version upgrades. I believe Apple's true strength lies in the advantage gained through its closed nature: stability.
(I've also heard stories of freezing occurring in some Apple apps. Is it the fate of smartphones..?)

**6. Finally, the question of whether touch is truly the ultimate device**
[Extreme articles even came out, stating that the mouse would disappear within 5 years due to the enthusiasm for iPhone touch](http://blog.naver.com/fstory97/70067073673), but I don't agree.
I'm not sure. I tend to think that the biggest bottleneck and difficulty in interfaces is text input, not menu selection, so QWERTY is still the most comfortable for me, which is why I switched to the X1. According to Jobs' philosophy, the iPhone probably won't have a QWERTY keyboard. In the past, there was talk of laser keyboards, and a certain research lab in Korea even demonstrated a Korean input method using a gyroscope sensor. Samsung's newly released phone introduced a text input method using touch called "Swipe," but I don't find it particularly intuitive yet. (Of course, there's no interface as unintuitive as QWERTY, yet I use it well.)

[Samsung's Swipe]

**However, the ultimate input device I desire is something that doesn't bother others (voice input is out here), is intuitive, allows input while driving without having to look at the actual screen, and achieves QWERTY speed without using both hands. I hope such a device emerges.**
But for now, nothing beats QWERTY for me. I heard that BlackBerry's QWERTY is better than the X1's... but due to my need to draw as mentioned above, BlackBerry was out because of its low resolution and LCD that doesn't support a stylus.

titleEn: IPTV: The Way Forward and Areas for
contentEn:
Recently, IPTV has developed significantly. The number of subscribers is increasing, and technical issues related to it are also growing considerably. However, for users, IPTV should establish itself as a service that is cheaper, more diverse, and richer than these technical issues. In particular, my biggest expectation for IPTV is that it establishes itself as a software and content distribution platform. A platform that is easier than Apple's App Store, replaces P2P, and can be easily used even by grandparents. And ultimately, I hope it eliminates the act of connecting a complex PC to a TV.
However, the path ahead seems very long. First, there's the content fee.

**1. I am concerned about expensive content fees and the resulting failure of content distribution platforms to become mainstream.**
I tried MyLGTV, which is known to be the cheapest among the three major providers (SK, KT, LG) in many aspects, but honestly, I couldn't even consider purchasing paid content. Watching a 3,500 won movie for 48 hours via TV is incomparable in competitiveness to P2P, let alone Daum's current DRM-free movie download service. It is certainly burdensome that an IPTV movie, which cannot offer anything that a movie theater can, is traded at such a price.
The case for animation was even worse. Only the first three episodes of a 20-minute animation are free. Animations can range from 13 episodes to dozens, and if you buy the rest at 300 won each, it's much more burdensome than a movie. If this continues, parents are likely to prevent their children from watching animations due to the cost. Viewing patterns for animation and drama are not actually that different. It feels excessively expensive compared to dramas that become free after just one week. It seems more appropriate to sell an entire season and provide a much longer viewing period than just 48 hours.
Music videos were even more unreasonable. 500 won for 48 hours? A DRM-free MP3 costs 600 won, and music videos are currently available for free on platforms like Naver Music. Simply put, if you calculate purchasing one movie per week, it's 14,000 won. If you use dramas and various other services, it easily exceeds tens of thousands of won, and I can't shake the feeling that this is similar to some services offered by mobile carriers. Consequently, it means it won't establish itself as a popular service. The expensive services of mobile carriers weren't bad in themselves. The cost of information consumption for a household is somewhat limited. Furthermore, an information consumption platform cannot develop if it doesn't reach a certain scale.
Let's look at the case of the App Store. If a cheap content distribution platform targeting the global market, like the App Store, penetrates Korean homes, expensive distribution platforms that targeted only a small number of domestic users will once again be ignored.
The current potential of IPTV should be viewed with a longer-term perspective, not as a business platform fixated on immediate profits, but as something that can become a new competitive edge for Korea.

**2. The path IPTV should take can be learned from internet portals.**
Currently, many people criticize internet portals, saying they're closed or whatever, but general users rarely pay for services. Nevertheless, internet portals are making money. Why? It's through advertising and distribution margins. While advertising is a typical TV model and can be considered similar, distribution margins are an area IPTV has not yet ventured into. Games, music concert tickets, books, shopping – there's an endless array of things IPTV can sell.
In nearby Japan, the power of multi-content can be seen in several animations. Well-made animations often sweep the world like a storm with figures, merchandise, and fan-made games. The same goes for Hollywood movies.
Let's consider one thing here. What is the Korean Wave in our country? The idea of simply attracting tourists is quite naive and primary. IPTV can become that multi-platform. And if this is developed into software and middleware and sold, this multi-content can be sold as a package anywhere in the world where there is internet.
Imagine watching IRIS, and then content related to IRIS, blooper reels, travel tickets, t-shirts, earrings, toy guns. Imagine an IPTV software that sells all of these. This software could even be burned onto a DVD and sold as is.

**3. I hope IPTV becomes a new competitive edge for Korea.**
As a software developer, my expectations for IPTV are indeed unique. Until now, software and content have lost competitiveness due to illegal distribution. And the domestic packaged game market met the unfortunate fate of disappearing entirely. However, online games offered a new possibility, thanks to the emergence of cheaper, more appropriately priced, and diverse service models. And it became a pillar industry that put Hangame, NC, and Nexon at the top of IT companies today.
IPTV will become a core service of BcN in the future. And I hope it becomes a new competitive edge for Korea and is sold worldwide. If it only pursues market share and immediate profits within Korea, that's as far as it will go. I sincerely hope it becomes a more developed industry.

titleEn: [Share] The Life of a Stray Cat
Legend of Dragonia Part 2, Chapter 1
contentEn:
{{IMG:1}}
The next evening, Melchizedek received an urgent report about Aysia from Deputy Commander Galab.
"The bandit group's name is Maga (Great Hammer). Their leader's name is Agal. In terms of size, they are the fourth or fifth largest bandit group in Petra. However, yesterday they reportedly attacked and defeated the stronghold of Aquila (Eagle), the second-largest bandit group.
And it is said that the power of those brought by Aysia, a recently recruited female bandit, was significant. These are presumed to be intelligence agents from the Kingdom of Ceres. As a result, the defeated bandit group has been incorporated into theirs, making them comparable in size to the largest bandit group, and they are reportedly planning to attack Ardon (Hunchback), the largest bandit group, soon. If they also achieve victory against Ardon (Hunchback) and expand their forces, it seems we will be at a disadvantage even if we combine both the intelligence agency and the security forces."
At his words, Melchizedek clutched his head as if in pain and asked again.
"What is the security situation in the surrounding cities and the movements of the Ceres Kingdom's intelligence agency?"
"After contacting the four major surrounding cities – Kadesh, Sardis, Samil, and Akkan – many of those suspected of being from the Ceres Kingdom's central intelligence branch have gone into hiding."
"So that was their target... Has no information been gathered about the head of the Ceres Kingdom's central intelligence branch?"
"No, there isn't. There's also a recent rumor that it's a woman..."
"It's as if they're deliberately trying to pin it on Aysia..."
Melchizedek sighed.
"But aren't you perhaps trusting Aysia too much?"
Galab then asked back, sounding somewhat concerned.
"An answer that's too obvious is often a trap."
"It could also be a trap designed to exploit that."
Galab immediately retorted, and then suddenly, it became noisy outside.
"What's going on!"
"Soldiers have arrived from Kadesh Castle."
An intelligence agent entered the tent and reported.
"Soldiers from Kadesh?"
Melchizedek, wondering what was happening, rushed out of the tent. Kadesh Castle was a military city where soldiers were rested before being sent to the front lines and then redeployed. Therefore, most of their soldiers were well-trained and strong, and its lord, Mithraim, led an elite knight order. And now, Mithraim himself had led his troops here. As a knight from a prestigious noble family, he was far superior to Melchizedek in rank and standing, so Melchizedek was surprised and went out to greet him.
“What brings you here, leaving your castle...”
However, Prince Zacchaeus appeared and answered before he could finish.
“Welcome. I've been waiting for you. These soldiers here don't seem to listen to me very well. So I called for you.”
Only then did Melchizedek realize that Prince Zacchaeus had summoned them.
“From now on, Mithraim's knight order will take over this mission instead of the intelligence agency.”
This time, Melchizedek could not ignore Zacchaeus as he had the previous night. Melchizedek felt that the already complicated situation was becoming even more entangled. After organizing his knight order at the encampment, Mithraim immediately began to interrogate Melchizedek.
“Intelligence Commander Melchizedek, report.”
Melchizedek already had a premonition that no matter what he reported, he would not hear anything good. He felt that the matter was already out of his hands. After reporting all the circumstances and enduring a long scolding, Melchizedek emerged from the tent with a bitter expression.
Just then, Dagmon came to find Melchizedek. He looked even worse than before and seemed to be drunk.
“Melchizedek, I'm sorry. I can't sleep. I keep having nightmares, either searching for Aysia or being killed by her."
"Your Highness, I apologize. The situation is turning for the worse right now. It's difficult if you're like this too. Please rest first."
Melchizedek felt a mix of anger and pity for Dagmon, who was acting this way in such a situation.
"Melchizedek. No, listen to me. Until recently, the world was like heaven because of Aysia, but now, without Aysia, it's hell. Aysia slept with my brother and tried to kill me. How could that angelic woman do such a thing?"
Dagmon clung to Melchizedek stubbornly.
"Your Highness, you seem very drunk."
Melchizedek was not in the mood to listen to his drunken rambling. However, Dagmon suddenly spoke.
“I have an order for you.”
"What order, Your Highness? I have almost no authority left."
Melchizedek replied with a skeptical voice.
“Find Aysia and kill her.”
“What?”
Melchizedek, doubting his ears, asked back in surprise.
“You mean kill Aysia, not bring her back?”
“Yes, *sob*. She is nothing but pain to me anymore. Kill her for the crime of humiliating a prince. If it's that, we can execute her summarily without needing to question her other crimes, can't we?”
Melchizedek said, dumbfounded.
“What are you saying? Kill Aysia? And for the crime of humiliating royalty? Your Highness, aren't you ashamed? Didn't you truly love Aysia?”
Then Dagmon laughed hollowly and said.
“Love. Yes, I loved her. I liked her more than anything. That's why I can't bear it anymore.”
“Your Highness, your judgment seems clouded right now. I will pretend I didn't hear that.”
At Melchizedek's reply, Dagmon flared up in anger.
“What! My judgment is clouded?"
"If my words offended you, I apologize."
However, Dagmon's anger, far from subsiding, began to rage even more fiercely.
"Yes. Melchizedek. You liked Aysia too, didn't you? Isn't it *your* judgment that's clouded? Anyone can see Aysia is a wicked woman now. Could it be that you, too, conspired with Aysia to do this to me?"
"How can you say such things! Your Highness, aren't you too drunk?"
At Dagmon's outrageous response, Melchizedek felt wronged and even angry.
"I'm not drunk. I'm perfectly fine! Don't take me for someone so drunk they can't tell right from wrong! Yes, now it's clear. You should look closely too. Aysia might have even slept with you, but don't trust that woman. Have you seen her acting? You can't deny she has the ability to completely deceive everyone."
Seeing Dagmon like that, Melchizedek felt utterly miserable. In the end, Melchizedek also spoke the words he had been holding back.
“Your Highness. You have lost your judgment due to jealousy and a sense of loss.”
At those words, Dagmon became furious and shouted, which eventually caused soldiers and even General Mithraim to come out and witness the situation.
“Melchizedek! Are you defying orders? Don't forget you are a soldier of the Kingdom of Laodicea. My request is simple! Don't make me a foolish prince anymore. Our soldiers must not die at Aysia's hands any longer because of my mistakes.”
With soldiers outside the intelligence agency and even Mithraim watching, he realized he could truly be accused of insubordination, but he had no intention of backing down.
“You are being too hasty.”
“I make the judgments, and I make the decisions. You know where Aysia is. Go now, take the soldiers, and kill Aysia. Even though she betrayed me, I would rather die than see Aysia captured by my brother and humiliated. You must resolve this before that happens.”
“No.”
Melchizedek flatly refused.
“There's no other way... Mithraim!”
Dagmon called Mithraim.
“Yes, Your Highness.”
Hearing Dagmon's voice, Mithraim, who had been watching, replied.
“From now on, Mithraim, I am giving you an order. Commander Melchizedek knows Aysia's location through her ring. Go immediately with Melchizedek, kill her, and bring her body to me. If anyone helps her, consider them spies of the Kingdom of Ceres and you may kill them all. And when you kill her, make sure Melchizedek does it. You are to supervise Melchizedek to ensure he carries out the order.”
"Your Highness!"
Melchizedek called out to the prince in surprise, but he no longer even responded to his words and turned away. Instead, Mithraim gave Melchizedek an order.
“It's the Prince's command! Let's go! Melchizedek. Assemble the soldiers!”
Melchizedek couldn't bring himself to move. Dagmon's expression, as he gave the final order, was already filled with madness. Melchizedek doubted if this was the same person he had known. He had never realized Dagmon could be so cruel.
"What are you doing, Melchizedek! Quickly, call the soldiers."
Only at Mithraim's loud roar did Melchizedek come to his senses and hastily replied.
"Yes! Yes, I understand."
He had once before seen a similar expression on Dagmon's face. It was the day Dagmon had brought in the soldier who killed an old man he respected. No, today's expression seemed even more terrifying and cruel than that day. It was the look of someone who had lost everything, with only venom remaining.
And as Melchizedek assembled the soldiers, he had a premonition that Dagmon had made yet another choice he would surely regret for the rest of his life.

titleEn: Google Holds the Fate of HTML5,
contentEn:
**1. What will replace Active X?**
**{{IMG:1}}**
I read an [article mentioning HTML5 as a technology to replace Active X](http://www.zdnet.co.kr/ArticleView.asp?artice_id=20091116182745). Many talk about Active X as if it's the original sin of the domestic internet environment, but why do banks need to use Active X? And can HTML5 truly surpass Flash, JavaFX, and Silverlight to proudly establish itself as the web's mainstream? As a web developer by profession, this is a fascinating topic.
So, the moment I first saw that article, I started looking into why Active X is truly necessary for payments and banking, and in what ways HTML5 could replace Active X. I found some good resources on DBGuide. (You can view them for free if you just sign up.)

| [Part 1 | Active X: From Swan to Ugly Duckling – Problems and Solutions | Jung Hee-yong](http://www.dbguide.net/know/know102001.jsp?mode=view&pg=1&idx=3187) |
| --- |
| [**Part 2 | Urgent Fix: Alternative Technologies for Public Certificates | Choi Sang-hoon**](http://www.dbguide.net/know/know102001.jsp?mode=view&pg=1&idx=3188) |
| [Part 3 | UI Replacement is My Job: UI Development Using Ajax | Park Young-rok](http://www.dbguide.net/comb/common/edit/1%BA%CE%20%7C%20%B9%E9%C1%B6%BF%A1%BC%AD%20%B9%CC%BF%EE%BF%C0%B8%AE%B7%CE%20%C0%FC%B6%F4%C7%D1%20%BE%D7%C6%BC%BA%EAX%20%B9%AE%C1%A6%BF%CD%20%C7%D8%B0%E1%B9%E6%BE%C8%20%7C%20%C1%A4%C8%F1%BF%EB) |
| [Part 4 | Beyond Active X: Functionality and Compatibility – XPCOM Development Strategy | Kim Min-soo](http://www.dbguide.net/know/know102001.jsp?mode=view&pg=1&idx=3190) |
| [Part 5 | MS's Alternative to Active X: How to Utilize Silverlight | Han Yong-hee](http://www.dbguide.net/know/know102001.jsp?mode=view&pg=1&idx=3191) |

However, if we think about this more fundamentally, all plugins except HTML5 are essentially threads forked by the browser. Therefore, it might be a matter of whether the browser supports the specific plugin or HTML5's specifications. The concept of a plugin is, after all, an extension of the browser's functionality.
Conversely, ActiveX is fundamentally a Windows Application rather than a browser extension, merely called by Internet Explorer. Just as you cannot run a Windows application on Linux, you cannot port ActiveX to OSes other than Windows. If you really wanted to, you'd install an OS VM Ware, larger than the browser itself, within the browser. You'd have to embed Windows as a plugin in Firefox. If that were possible, if ActiveX could have been a plugin like Silverlight from the start, there would have been no discussion about ActiveX.

**3. The Baton Passes to the Browser... And the Destination is Google**
Ultimately, who will take the future standard will be determined by **how well browsers support those plugins** and **how many sites actually use that technology?** Thinking this way, Google is the company that has secured both of these.
**1) Chrome Browser + Google Web Services**
**{{IMG:2}}**
Similar to Naver's market share in Korea, Google's global market share is very high. Also, technologies used by Google tend to quickly become standards. Ajax for map services and Flash video plugins for YouTube became the standard for map services of domestic portals and for UCC sites. Therefore, Google can be considered the biggest decision-maker in determining who wins this game.

**2) One more for good measure! Chrome Browser + Google Web Services + Mobile Platform Android**
**{{IMG:3}}**
At the heart of this web standard issue is not Mac, but mobile platforms. The iPhone, which put wireless internet on track, is also a mobile platform created by Apple, and Google's Android is poised to step into this arena, with victory almost certain.
Mobile is becoming an issue in the next generation of web, expanding into an entirely new market. This ultimately means that the higher the mobile platform's market share, the easier it is to increase browser market share.
Similar to IE's market share on Windows, Chrome's market share on Android will be a natural phenomenon. Android's smartphone market share in the future is very positive, and currently, it can be said to have no rivals.

**3) Google's Competitors**
Samsung's Bada has no web service model and no browser. Apple, being a single model, will find it difficult to exceed 20% of the market, unlike Android which releases new models almost every month.
For Microsoft, the traditional powerhouse of mobile platforms, recovering the reliability of Windows Mobile seems most important. Up to the existing 6.5, reliability is still lacking, and there's a need for a reliable and efficient mobile OS like Windows 7 for the public; the ability to use PC-based IE is a strength. If pushed, there's a possibility of some compatibility with Active-X. If so, it could be a very good solution in Korea, but perfect compatibility is unlikely, so it's hard to expect much. Above all, its web influence is very low compared to Google, putting it at a disadvantage.
Flash has been the most successful so far, but with companies like Google, MS, and SUN, which have undeniable scale and strengths, emerging as competitors, it's uncertain how well they will manage to secure the market. However, their strength is having the most content (games). The reason Apple doesn't want to put Flash on the iPhone, I suspect, is ultimately to prevent the App Store from being hit by Flash. (Jobs saying Flash is too heavy to run on the iPhone is a lie. Flash runs on phones with worse specs.)

**[Hangame Flash game 'Gogunbuntu' gained huge popularity]**

**4. What will domestic portals do? The technical standard is still Google.**
To cut a long story short, Google is currently considered the standard for web technology. In Korea, too, it has been a situation where if Google does something, Naver follows, and if Naver does something, other portals follow, so this is expected to remain valid.
**1) Google's HTML5 Support ([http://ddobagi.textcube.com/57])**
Since [Google is interested in HTML5](http://ddobagi.textcube.com/57), it's uncertain if HTML5 will truly become mainstream. If Google, with its market share in Android and Chrome, releases a brilliant RIA using HTML5, everyone will follow that technology, and its market share will increase significantly in a short time. Flash, Silverlight, and JavaFX still give the impression of needing to install something, so they ultimately have the inherent disadvantage of not being a standard.

{{IMG:4}}
**[Flash is not a true standard!]**
In fact, these technologies, which are not standards but merely widely ported, are not in a position to criticize ActiveX. If Google can just demonstrate sufficiently easy libraries and brilliant technical demonstrations using HTML5, the perception of HTML5 will change instantly, and books about HTML5 will flood the market.

**2) HTML5 is currently sluggish compared to other solutions**
Currently, no company is readily adopting HTML5 compared to other solutions, because there's a lack of supporting browsers, few technical references for development, and no tangible services that resonate. If this continues, HTML5 will have no room to squeeze in among other already established technologies. Therefore, the fate of this technology seems to be determined by Google's HTML5 support services within the period Google secures its mobile market share, i.e., within the next 3 years.

**In conclusion, Google is the neighborhood boss of the internet industry. OTL.**
**{{IMG:5}}**
**[Unifying the web is a piece of cake for Google]**

titleEn: IPTV vs. Portal vs. P2P:
contentEn:
Recently, there have been strong calls for the normalization of the video content market. With Korean films gaining popularity and home theaters becoming widespread, we must avoid following in the footsteps of Korea's packaged game market. Therefore, I will compare P2P, which has historically been at the forefront of illegal distribution, with the recently expanding IPTV, and the newly launched download services from portals.

| Category | IPTV {{IMG:1}} | Internet Portal {{IMG:2}} | P2P {{IMG:3}} |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Description | A business launched by broadcasters using internet technology, connecting directly to a TV to watch broadcasts. A major advantage is the ability to watch terrestrial real-time content. | Started by portals, which have the majority of internet users as subscribers, in conjunction with filmmakers and the 'Good Downloader' campaign to normalize the download market. | Began with Soribada's MP3 distribution, recognized as a traditional channel for illegal content distribution, allowing large amounts of data to be distributed cheaply. |
| Major Operators | 3 major telecom companies (SK, LG, KT) | Portal operators (Naver, Daum, Paran) | Small and medium P2P operators (Pruna, MFile, Xtoc, Fileguri, etc.) |
| In terms of operator size, the order is IPTV, Portal, P2P. | | | |
| Subscribers | Relatively average | Relatively many | Relatively few |
| Currently, portals have the most subscribers, but telecom subscribers are rapidly flowing into IPTV, showing significant growth. P2P users are relatively fewer in number, but they often act as power users and digital hubs, leading to a large ripple effect. | | | |
| Pricing | New releases 3500 won ~ Free DRM (48 hours) | New releases 3500 won ~ 500 won DRM (present/absent) | Under 500 won (packet, subscription billing) |
| IPTV has no means to transfer files to other mobile devices and is most strongly blocked by DRM. For portals, the lack of free content is a drawback, while Daum's lack of DRM is an advantage. P2P is superior in price competitiveness by several times, causing other methods to lose their competitive edge in the content transaction market. This is because P2P operators do not pay copyright fees for illegally distributed content. | | | |
| Content Volume | Average | Few | Many |
| P2P, with active user participation, has the most diverse content, while portal operators, being the latest entrants, have the fewest. | | | |
| Content Acquisition Speed | Average | Average | Very fast |
| In the case of P2P, users rip the content they want, so content acquisition speed is very fast. Other services that require copyright negotiation are much slower, and it's difficult for them to match the diversity. Especially for foreign dramas and animations, P2P shows an overwhelmingly faster acquisition. To secure competitiveness for legal services like IPTV or portals, increasing the volume and acquisition speed of content is very important. After all, there are users who download content because they find waiting for IPTV bothersome. | | | |
| User Accessibility | Excellent | Good | Low |
| IPTV has no burden of turning on a PC; P2P sites involve the hassle of navigating to minor sites and accessing communities. | | | |
| Search | Low | Excellent | Good |
| The biggest problem with IPTV is that searching is not easy. The remote control is inconvenient and slow compared to a keyboard, and the poor search UI makes it very inconvenient compared to internet sites, which seems to be an area that needs urgent improvement. Portals, traditional search powerhouses, are expected to provide diverse and powerful search services by linking with integrated search. For P2P, many words are filtered due to copyright issues, but users access desired content and communities by circumventing these filters in various ways. While copyright filtering is a major inconvenience, searches are conducted by exploiting the weaknesses of search filters. (Harry Potter -> H.a.r.r.y P.o.t.t.e.r -> Hally Potter) | | | |
| Adult Content | Weak | Weak | Strong |
| Recently, Japan raised a copyright dispute with Korea over adult content, but ultimately, the copyright was not recognized. This content, often called 'yadon' (porn) unlike typical R-rated films, is a primary source of revenue for P2P sites. To fundamentally eradicate P2P, the copyright issue of adult content must be addressed even more vigorously than that of films. Youth protection measures remain only on portals and IPTV, and P2P is a complete blind spot. If we are to tackle illegal content distribution, adult content is precisely what must be addressed. | | | |
| UCC Support | Limited utilization | Extensive utilization | None |
| UCC fundamentally started in a web environment, so it shows the most utilization on the web. However, revenue sharing for producers is not happening for all, and IPTV offers limited UCC services in conjunction with portals. P2P can be said to be a service far removed from UCC. | | | |
| Mobile Support | None | Limited support | Content acquisition by users |
| For mobile devices, files cannot be moved externally due to DRM, making IPTV completely unable to support them. Portals offer some support in MP4 format but do not provide various formats suitable for different devices. P2P sees mobile content produced and distributed by users, centered around communities for mobile device playback. With the rise of smartphones like DivX-compatible phones and iPhones, the need for mobile video playback is expected to grow as much as MP3s. | | | |
| Future Development Direction | Leveraging its strength as the most accessible home appliance, it has a high potential to transform into the easiest media distribution platform. It's easy to secure traditional broadcast content, and it's expected to have separate specifications for mobile IPTV. | It has high potential to develop into web TV and is most accessible to internet users. If mobile full browsing becomes possible and a seamless, inexpensive wireless environment is established, it is expected to be utilized as an app or a separate mobile application. Additionally, its strengths include the ability to link with many other internet services and possessing a powerful user database. | To shed its stigma of illegal content distribution, some copyrighted paid content is being sold, but its utilization is not high, and accessibility is lower compared to IPTV or portals. Many legal restrictions are expected in the future, and a new business model for P2P technology itself is needed. |

**Conclusion**
Currently, both portals and IPTV operators directly negotiate all copyrights, but in such cases, distribution volume and speed are inevitably slower than P2P. Therefore, I believe it would be appropriate for the content distribution market to adopt a 'Mall in Mall' approach, where relevant companies provide distribution and search platforms. The number of foreign dramas and animations will naturally far exceed what the three major broadcasters distribute. And I hope that adult content, too, will be distributed within the institutional framework, rather than being indiscriminately exposed to teenagers in the shadows.
Regardless of the service, the content distribution market must be normalized for the sake of our cultural industry. However, we cannot ignore the current state of the market. I hope that good services and legislation will emerge to change the current market trends.

titleEn: [Extreme Taekwondo Musical Performance] Tat
contentEn:
http://shopping.naver.com/detail/detail.nhn?cat_id=12090003&nv_mid=5456372278&tc=3
[Show Title: Tata IN Buddha - Extreme Taekwondo](http://shopping.naver.com/detail/detail.nhn?cat_id=12090003&nv_mid=5456372278&tc=3)
[Musical Period: October 17 ~ November 22, 2009](http://shopping.naver.com/detail/detail.nhn?cat_id=12090003&nv_mid=5456372278&tc=3)
[Time: Tue-Thu 8:00 PM / Fri 5:30 PM, 8:30 PM / Sat 2:30 PM, 5:30 PM, 8:30 PM / Sun 2:30 PM, 5:30 PM / Mon Closed](http://shopping.naver.com/detail/detail.nhn?cat_id=12090003&nv_mid=5456372278&tc=3)
[Genre: Musical](http://shopping.naver.com/detail/detail.nhn?cat_id=12090003&nv_mid=5456372278&tc=3)
[Venue: National Theater of Korea KB Youth Sky Theater](http://shopping.naver.com/detail/detail.nhn?cat_id=12090003&nv_mid=5456372278&tc=3)
[Cast: Lim Chun-gil, Jeon Su-mi, Lee Rang, Oh Hyung-gyun, Jung Il-sung](http://shopping.naver.com/detail/detail.nhn?cat_id=12090003&nv_mid=5456372278&tc=3)
 
 

 
 The plot was generally very simple. In fact, I only realized at the very end of the musical that 'Buddha' referred to the Buddha. I had just been thinking of it as 'Extreme Taekwondo.' No wonder I kept hearing the name 'Siddhartha'... Gautama Siddhartha was indeed the Buddha's original name. Anyway, it was only when I saw the scene at the end where a pattern presumed to be a Bodhi tree rose from behind that I realized this story was about Buddha... I was quite foolish. {{IMG:1}}
 
**1. My first question here was: Why Taekwondo and Buddha?**
 http://llf.or.kr/04info/design_view.asp?search=&searchV=&bm_code=72&order=T&h_seq=37&page=3&order_key=&order_type=  
 [Taekwondo Baby Buddha: Image Source: [http://llf.or.kr](http://llf.or.kr/) ]
 
** 1) A famous subject choice aimed at an international audience?**
 There will likely be differing opinions on why the story of Buddha was chosen for Taekwondo, a thoroughly Korean subject. However, I could infer the intention from Baek Jae-hyun's explanation. The talk of targeting Las Vegas, and thus the world, ultimately means selling an image. Frankly, Buddhism, which many people worldwide already know, would be much more effective for an oriental image than our lesser-known history. It's an undeniable fact that Taekwondo and Buddhism are already more famous than the name 'Korea.' If possible, **it would have been better to tell a Korean story... (Korea has so many wonderful stories... and if not, making it like Japan isn't a bad method either.)** But considering an international audience, it was a somewhat understandable choice of subject. 
**** 
** 2) A wrong choice for the domestic market**
However, considering that a quarter of Korea is close to fundamentalist Christianity and they might have prejudices against Buddhist stories, it seems hard to view this as a good choice. Surely, one cannot abandon the domestic market? Furthermore, compared to Christian culture, which is already active with CCM and musicals, the production and distribution of Buddhist culture have less experience, and cultural consumption by followers is extremely small. From a purely domestic perspective, it seems like a worse choice than using traditional Korean subjects. Shouldn't it gain some traction domestically before going abroad?
**** 
** 3) The excessive gap between the young prince and the religious saint in the story**
**{{IMG:2}}**
[Image Source: [http://cafe.naver.com/movie02/117771](http://imagesearch.naver.com/detail/frame_top_080722.html#) ]

 Furthermore, the Bodhi tree that appeared at the end was a scene where the young prince, who had opened his eyes to the world, suddenly became a religious saint, but it was a very unkind development for the audience. A religious person might know the middle part of the story, but the abrupt reversal without any intermediate explanation left me bewildered. Did Buddha attain enlightenment through Tata's story? Why did the prince suddenly become a religious saint? If it was created for a global audience, the answer cannot be found just by watching this play. Not many American citizens in Las Vegas would have detailed information about Buddha. Rather, if it's a story about a prince understanding the world, there's already one in the West: Andersen's famous fairy tale, 'The Prince and the Pauper.' But did that prince attain enlightenment? Wouldn't it be more common to think he should have governed better? If the final scene had been omitted entirely, or if it had concluded with a kind narration about the story afterward, people like me, who knew nothing, would have been intrigued enough to search for 'Buddha' and learn about his birth, instead of being confused. In fact, not knowing that Buddha was the Buddha, I expected him to become a great king, which might have made the plot twist even more surprising.
 
** 4) How will the world perceive this?**
 Buddhism is, in fact, already associated with a specific martial art image worldwide: Shaolin Temple. It's arguably so famous that it might even be more well-known than 'Korea,' so I wonder if there's room for Taekwondo to fit in. If people watch the play without prior information, wouldn't more of them see it as one of the Shaolin martial arts? Furthermore, for globalization, 'Tata in Buddha' might be uncomfortable for Indians, a population of over a billion. If a traditional martial art from the distant East is inserted into costumes that don't look Indian (I thought they looked Sumerian based on the costumes alone), they might even feel displeasure. Wouldn't it feel as strange to them as telling Admiral Yi Sun-sin's story with Capoeira? They would likely believe that Buddha's story should be told with Kalaripayattu.
 
**2. The boy's miscasting, surprisingly often pointed out**
 It seems I wasn't the only one who felt a sense of incongruity with the pretty-faced boy's voice. The problem wasn't that the actress playing the boy couldn't act. It wasn't a cross-dressing male character like Queen Seondeok, but rather an overly pretty face, a slender physique, and then a jarringly deep boy's voice. To reconcile these two, one of them has to break. If there isn't a suitably plain actor, wouldn't it be better to change the voice actor? It's common for women to voice boys in animation because boys have a somewhat neutral image. Or, perhaps, changing the role to a girl wouldn't cause a major problem in the story. A girl might even garner more sympathy.
 
**3. Songs lacking variety compared to the performance**
 Jeon Su-mi's singing was powerful and excellent, but with only one person singing, it felt very much like her stage, and the rest were more like backup dancers. Of course, it's impossible to do Taekwondo and sing at the same time, but it would have been nice to hear songs with various voices, even if it was lip-synced. There was also the drawback that it was a bit difficult to hear the lyrics, possibly due to sound issues.
 
**3. The supporting characters lacked humor.**
 Given the heavy theme, there should have been enough comedic elements... but they seemed somewhat lacking. The importance of comedic characters and supporting roles is like seasoning in food. Without it, something feels empty, and it enhances the main flavor, but 'Tata in Buddha' lacked this. In the case of 'Maria Maria,' which dealt with a similar religious theme, the flavorful roles of the supporting characters were quite significant, so joy was not missing among the emotions. However, 'Tata in Buddha' felt too heavy overall. Usually, in heavier plays, such roles become even more crucial. I wondered if including a bit of comedy and strengthening the supporting roles would have intensified the contrasting feeling of sorrow.
 
**4. Nevertheless, a spectacular performance just by being Taekwondo**
**    And excellent acting, though not by professionals** 
**** **Nevertheless, it was worth watching. The exquisite, spectacular, and disciplined movements made me exclaim, 'As expected, Taekwondo!'** and deserved generous applause. Of course, one or two board breaks missed their mark (but the two main actors were, needless to say, perfection itself. Buddha's character had a gentle yet strong impression, and Tata's character had a strong, wild charm. They were also characters women would like...). However, even those minor mistakes were understandable given the difficulty and speed of the movements. Kicking the boards without them flying into the audience must also be challenging, but they did it very well. Above all, I wanted to give high marks to the actors' effort and passion. There was no great difficulty in empathizing.
 
**5. Good idea: Board autograph session**
 Board breaking is indispensable in a Taekwondo performance, and selling autographed boards was a good idea, a unique element that only 'Tata in Buddha' could have. My spouse and I also bought one and got autographs on our way out.
 
**6. Interest in the globalization of Korean musicals. Tata in Buddha, which must grow with advice**
**{{IMG:3}}
** There were many parts of Baek Jae-hyun's story that I empathized with. Our actors and cultural content naturally grow with interest and love. And 'Tata in Buddha' could become a meaningful work in many ways: the cultural content-ification of Taekwondo. **However, I think the comments about Baek Jae-hyun's negative reviews found through an internet search were a bit hasty.** It's difficult for content to satisfy everyone's needs. And if there's no interest, one wouldn't write a long post in the first place.

**I hope that good Korean themes like Taekwondo, along with passion and excellent actors, can reach a wider stage.** To do so, the voices of domestic audiences must be heard to some extent. This is because they are also customers, their money serves as a foundation for global expansion, and they point out weaknesses and strengths.
It was regrettable that there were many empty seats due to the H1N1 flu, but their efforts achieved this much. However, they must not stop there.
**As Tata-in Buddha is not a professional, there are clearly still shortcomings, much like unfinished performers. Therefore, I believe they can still change and grow. And, audiences will probably respond to it someday.**

**Overall, it's a great performance to enjoy a wonderful show without spending a huge amount of money. Highly recommended for those who love martial arts and for men!! The last part might be easier to understand for those with deep Buddhist faith. I wrote about the shortcomings, but it was a performance with so much to see that there were also many regrettable aspects. Just go see it~!**

**ps. Why doesn't Naver have a performance database?**

titleEn: Our Third Wedding Anniversary Namsan Date Story
contentEn:
{{IMG:1}}
		
		
	
		
			

#### Namsan

			
			Namsan  
			
		
		Period 2009.11.4 ~ 2009.11.4 (1 day)
		Concept Romantic Couple's Trip
		Route 
		Bundang → National Theater → N Seoul Tower → National Theater  
		
	
	
				

	
		
		
		
	Hearing that I hadn't prepared anything for our wedding anniversary, I hastily woke up early and planned an itinerary. I booked tickets for the Tata in Buddha performance at Namsan using Yes24 coins. Coincidentally, there was a big discount, so R-seats were 18,000 won each. I also searched for nearby restaurants and secured our travel route. After registering the schedule on Naver Calendar, I sent a schedule sharing request to my wife's email.

I used Oasis to leave work a bit early, and my wife arrived on time with the car in front of my company in Bundang. I gave her a single rose I had bought during lunchtime (Looking closely, I realized the florist had tricked me. ㅜㅜ One of the petals was damaged, and they say flowers are cut short these days to make them easier to carry, but my wife didn't like it. I deeply regretted not choosing the flower myself. Could cutting them short also be a way to save on packaging materials?)

Sitting in the driver's seat, I immediately drove straight to Namsan, our planned date spot. Around 5 PM, I was worried the traffic at Yangjae and Seocho ICs on the Gyeongbu Expressway might derail our plans. However, other than that, we drove smoothly and arrived at Namsan in 45 minutes.

 What we ordered at Sweetree, which I found through a Naver search, was cream spaghetti and sirloin steak, chosen by my wife who disliked expensive course meals, totaling 52,000 won. I didn't have a KTF discount card, but since it was a special day, I decided to just pay. Fortunately, I had a Happy21 gift certificate, so I only paid 22,000 won.
 Perhaps because it was an early weekday evening at 6 PM, there weren't many people, so making a reservation didn't feel particularly worthwhile. We sat at a table with a good view, but the seats felt a bit too close together, and the children behind us were distracting, so we gave up the view and moved to a quieter spot. The food was excellent, just as I had read online. According to my wife, the revolving restaurant at the top of Seoul Tower was expensive and truly terrible. I wished Sweetree had more private spaces and slightly dimmer lighting. If the lighting is too bright, both the candlelight on the table and the night view outside lose their charm. When I tried to take pictures out the window with my automatic camera, it only captured the shadows of the interior reflected in the bright lights, making me miss my broken DSLR even more. Nevertheless, the food was excellent, and with our human eyes, superior to any camera, we enjoyed the night view and had dinner for about an hour, taking a [proof shot](http://me2day.net/fstory/2009/11/04#18:40:01).
{{IMG:19}}{{IMG:20}}
 Tata-in Buddha had received a 30,000 won discount, but the condition was to bring a mask for the H1N1 prevention campaign. The problem was that I only remembered this after arriving at Namsan, and there are no pharmacies on Namsan. The convenience store at Seoul Tower only sold children's masks. Feeling a bit uneasy, I decided to take the circulating bus and buy one in the city center on the way back to the National Theater, as the bus route passes through there again. The wind was chilly during the few minutes we waited for the bus.
 The journey back to the National Theater seemed to take a bit longer because we went through the city center.

My wife, who loves dogs, got off on the street in front of Daehan Cinema where there's a pet shop, looked at the puppies for a bit, and bought masks at a pharmacy.

Using a gift certificate won from a Me2day widget event, we ordered two cafe lattes at Starbucks, but there were more people than expected, so it became 10 minutes before the 8 PM show. Thanks to a driver who was a former racer, we arrived back at the National Theater in 5 minutes. (Taxi fare: 2800 won).

Perhaps due to the H1N1 flu on a weekday evening, there weren't many people. We had booked R-seats at the very front, so I was satisfied, thinking we'd get a good view of the actors' faces. But lo and behold... the R-seats weren't really R-seats. Being close wasn't all good; it was a side view, so the characters were obscured. I thought I should have listened to Baek Jae-hyun's suggestion to move seats before the show started. Crucially, some man who came in during the performance sat in our row and kept shaking his chair, so we ended up moving seats in the middle of the play.[I plan to post about the performance again](http://blog.naver.com/fstory97/70073548971).

Admiring the spectacular Taekwondo performance, and Jeon Su-mi's explosive vocal power, time quickly passed. I felt sorry for the theater company, but I considered it lucky to have seen the performance cheaply, perhaps due to the H1N1 flu. On the way out, we got the actors' autographs on a wooden board and returned home.
On the way back, we stopped by Beomgye Station, bought Jjamppong, Japchae-bap, and Makgeolli, and finished the day at home. That night, we fell asleep without any 'incidents' (?), and our third wedding anniversary passed just like that. I wonder if it would be difficult to spend our fourth wedding anniversary like this if we have a child.

ps. Naver Maps, with its route insertion and enhanced public transport, is all good, but inserting routes into a blog seems a bit inconvenient.

titleEn: An AR Mobile Game You Play by Running/Walking
contentEn:
[Nintendo DSi game where you meet ghosts in augmented reality... Ghostwire](http://www.neoearly.net/2463575)
 

[This file does not support direct playback. Click to play in a pop-up window.](http://blog.naver.com/ObjectHttpView.naver?blogId=fstory97&logNo=70072894392&hashKey=ce7d9cf4f48f897867edb627ea62edd5)
Source: [http://www.neoearly.net/2463575](http://www.neoearly.net/2463575)
 
This is a cool augmented reality game I saw on Radio Kids' blog.
 It's similar to a concept I had in mind: playing a game by walking around the real world offline and finding specific tags. (I've submitted the idea to my company, but I'll make it public if it's rejected. My company isn't related to games, so it's highly likely to be rejected. ^^;)
 
 The world we live in becomes the game's field. You meet NPCs everywhere and solve the game.
 It seems like it could be a good concept that goes beyond the prejudice that mobile games turn people into hikikomori, encouraging players to run around and enjoy the game.
