contentEn:
{{IMG:1}}

Dagmon tried to sleep in his tent but couldn't. After hearing about today's events from Melchizedek, he was too furious to bear it. He wanted to grab a sword and cut down his brother immediately.
In the end, Dagmon pulled out a strong liquor and emptied a bottle in one go. However, his head only ached severely, and sleep still wouldn't come. Frustrated, Dagmon let out a cry of "Ugh!" from his bed and got up. He decided he'd rather wake Melchizedek and have another drink.
Dagmon went to Melchizedek's tent. A light was on, as if he hadn't slept yet, and the murmur of people talking could be heard. Dagmon called out to Melchizedek and was about to enter the tent when he froze at the sound coming from inside. Inside, Melchizedek was drinking alcohol poured by his young attendant.
“So, you're saying the captain gave a ring to Lady Aysia? Are you crazy? What kind of ring is that?”
“Hahaha. You're right. I must be crazy.”
“Oh dear~ Just tell her you like her, Captain, you big dummy.”
“How can I do that? Aysia belongs to the Prince! Stop talking nonsense and fill my glass. It's empty, isn't it? Oh, do you want a drink too?”
“Captain. If you were a normal adult, you'd tell me I'm still too young to drink, wouldn't you?”
“Do I look like a normal adult to you?”
“Sigh. Well, I guess not. You're a grown-up kid. Honestly, is Aysia even suitable for the Prince? The ending is obviously going to be bad anyway. Ask anyone. The love between a gypsy girl and a prince~ Ah~ So romantic. But just think for a moment. What kind of ending would such a story have? A happy ending lacks realism. Realism, you know?”
“Oh. You. Haven't you lost your dreams too early for your age? Have you never dreamed of a beautiful princess falling in love with you?”
“Even if I can't drink, I'm past the age for fairy tales.”
“Sigh... Yes... Fairy tales. Fairy tales. But my love is just as unrealistic. I can't possibly approach Aysia. I can only watch her. Well, that's good in its own way... but what can I do about this aching in my heart?”
Dagmon was utterly shocked to learn that Melchizedek liked Aysia. Realizing that the man he had considered merely a good friend was in love with his woman, he felt an inexplicable sense of discomfort towards him. While he understood that anyone his age could fall for someone, the fact that it was Aysia... that, somehow, he couldn't accept. Moreover, the conversation about his and Aysia's love being unrealistic was even more shocking. This made him feel, for some reason, distrustful of Melchizedek.
“We're out of liquor. I'll go get more.”
Melchizedek's attendant, who was going out to get more liquor, was about to leave the tent when he spotted a frozen Dagmon.
“Prince Dagmon!”
The boy, startled, bowed to the prince, and at the child's cry, Melchizedek sobered up instantly. Dagmon silently entered the tent and, with a stern expression, ordered the boy to bring more liquor.
“My apologies, Melchizedek. I didn't know about your feelings...”
“I'm sorry...”
“What is there to be sorry about? Can a person's heart be controlled? Aysia must indeed be a beauty.”
Dagmon offered Melchizedek a drink with a bitter expression.
“However, it seems I cannot entrust Aysia's matter to you after all. If you like her, can you truly remain impartial to personal feelings? And it would be painful for you to watch from the sidelines.”
“No, sir. That won't happen.”
Melchizedek strongly denied it, but Dagmon, with a hardened expression, briefly stated his opinion.
“I'm sorry.”
Melchizedek understood the underlying meaning of Dagmon's firm words but couldn't refute them. Dagmon no longer trusted him. Melchizedek felt that things were becoming increasingly complicated and difficult, and the liquor he was drinking, though truly bitter, strangely didn't make him drunk.
How long did Melchizedek endure that uncomfortable drinking session? Eventually, Dagmon began to get angry.
“Melchizedek! How could you! You also think Aysia and I won't work out, don't you?”
“How could that be? Your Highness seems to be very drunk.”
“No... I'm not drunk. *sob sob*...”
This time, Dagmon suddenly started crying.
“Aysia... my poor love... *sob*. Because of me...”
Watching him, Melchizedek felt a surge of anger, but unable to express it, he instead comforted Dagmon.
“Everything will be alright, Your Highness. Surely.”
However, Dagmon didn't reply; instead, he buried his head and didn't get up. Having drunk too much, he succumbed to the alcohol and fell asleep. Seeing this, Melchizedek sighed deeply, poured another drink into his glass, and muttered to himself.
“I truly envy you, who has everything.”

Time was nearing dawn, a time when even the soldiers on guard duty at the supply base found it hard to fight off sleep. Just a few hours ago, there had been a noisy commotion caused by Prince Zacchaeus, but now the camp was excessively quiet. The night sky had grown cloudy, as the stars had noticeably diminished, and fog had begun to descend.
There were five soldiers guarding the tent where the nomadic women were held. One of them was a young intelligence soldier on duty, and the other four were supply base soldiers waiting for the next shift. They had lit a bonfire to warm themselves and were gathered together, passing the idle time with conversation.
“So, you're saying you set fire to the Ceres Kingdom's supply base in that battle?”
“Yes, that's right. Of course, the intelligence deputy commander was with me, but I was the one who first set the fire. Thanks to that, ten thousand Ceres Kingdom soldiers had to retreat against our three thousand.”
As the young intelligence soldier boasted and recounted his heroic tales, the other soldiers were impressed.
“You were truly amazing for your age.”
The supply base soldiers in the rear generally had little experience in combat, so they were impressed even by the young intelligence soldier's boasts, and the intelligence soldier, feeling proud, began to tell increasingly grander tales.
“This time, you see, I infiltrated Brugia Castle in Ceres.”
Just then, a rustling sound came from beyond the fog. Instantly, the soldiers stopped talking and reflexively drew their swords. A human-like shadow appeared in the fog.
“Who goes there!”
The fog was so thick that they couldn't easily identify the figures with their eyes, so they first asked for their identities, and fortunately, a reply came from the shadows.
“We are the next shift.”
Only then did the soldiers lower their guard and grumble.
“Ugh~ Why are you only just arriving now! You're ten minutes late.”
“We were delayed because of an order from Prince Zacchaeus on the way.”
“Oh, what was it about?”
“Prince Zacchaeus ordered us to bring a woman named Aysia to his tent.”
“Lady Aysia?”
The intelligence soldier was startled by his words, as he had received a special order from Melchizedek to protect Aysia. One of the relief soldiers entered the tent where the nomadic women were, without giving anyone a chance to stop him.
“Wait. Just a moment. I need to report this to Captain Melchizedek.”
Then another soldier from the relief shift said,
“I apologize, but we are not part of the intelligence unit. We are simply soldiers of the Kingdom of Laodicea, and in our chain of command, we have no choice but to obey if the Prince commands. If we delay, only our heads will roll.”
The young intelligence soldier couldn't find a reason to stop them from taking Aysia. He decided he had to inform Melchizedek of this fact immediately and began to run towards Melchizedek's tent.

As soon as the soldier entered the tent to find Aysia, someone inside lit a small lantern. A woman was sitting fully dressed, as if she had been waiting.
Illuminated by the lantern, she wore a strange smile. The woman was Deborah. Deborah was dressed in Aysia's clothes and had styled her hair like Aysia's. Without any sign of surprise, as if it had been prearranged, the soldier led Deborah, dressed as Aysia, out of the tent.
“On your way back to the encampment, escort this lady to Prince Zacchaeus.”
The soldier handed Deborah over to the soldiers returning to their quarters. Deborah kept her head bowed low, avoiding eye contact with the other soldiers.
“Understood.”
“This woman is suspected of being a spy, so she might not be an ordinary person. Be careful, as she might try to escape midway. Make sure to bring her safely to the Prince.”
“Don't worry. It's funnier for one woman to be escorted by four men. Thanks to this, we're just losing out on precious sleep.”
The soldiers took Deborah and headed towards Zacchaeus's tent.

At that moment, the young intelligence soldier was running towards Melchizedek's quarters. Suddenly, his leg went numb, causing him to stumble and fall.
'Damn it, to be so foolish at a time like this...'
He tried to get up and run again, but his numb leg wouldn't move as he wished, which he found strange. He felt something warm suddenly flowing from his leg. Coming to his senses, he looked at his leg again and saw a dagger stuck in his shin. The numbness quickly turned into excruciating pain.
At that moment, realizing it was a night raid, he tried to scream, but a strong blow to the back of his neck choked him, and he fell forward. Another dagger was plunged into the back of his neck, and blood gushed out like a fountain. He died without even identifying his enemy.
"We have brought a woman named Aysia, as ordered by Prince Zacchaeus."
The four soldiers who arrived in front of Prince Zacchaeus's tent handed over Deborah, disguised as Aysia, to the soldiers guarding the prince.
"Good grief. This prince fellow calls for women day in and day out. Today she was carried in, so I thought she was quietly sleeping, but anyway, I understand."
The guard soldier let Deborah into the tent. And behind the tent, there was an eye secretly watching the scene. He was also an intelligence soldier, monitoring Prince Zacchaeus under Melchizedek's orders. Although the fog made it difficult to discern the woman's face, he confirmed Aysia's attire and immediately headed to Melchizedek's tent.

titleEn: Various Value-Added Services Beyond IPTV Broadcasting
contentEn:
**1. There's more to do than just broadcasting! Value-added services**
One of the good things about using IPTV is the variety of value-added services available. In the case of MyLGTv, it offers education, leisure, karaoke, games, and more. The billing method is typically a daily usage fee.
{{IMG:1}}
[ My LG TV Karaoke billing method ]

When running such programs, there is a slight delay when switching from live broadcast to a value-added service.
{{IMG:2}}
[ Of course, it's much shorter than Windows boot time, but it would have been better if they showed an advertisement. ]

This delay means that IPTV, rather than being just a broadcast, requires loading time, similar to a computer. These applications are actually implemented as Java or Flash applications, just like on a computer. The fact that IPTV can run these general-purpose platforms means that it can provide any application, as long as the specifications support it. The problem, however, is that current IPTV specifications are inferior to those of PCs or mobile phones.

**1) Games and Karaoke on IPTV**
{{IMG:3}}
[ My LG TV's Karaoke service ]

Among the programs I've used on IPTV, games and karaoke had high satisfaction. While flashy 3D games don't run yet, the environment was sufficient for board games like Go-Stop.
And if you're using IPTV as a media bay, as I mentioned before, you can enjoy karaoke with excellent sound quality. However, the lack of built-in microphone support is a drawback for using it solely as a karaoke machine. It was quite difficult to sing without anything when sober. Song updates are almost real-time as they are provided by Kumyoung, a professional karaoke company, and you can find songs on their website or search using the IPTV remote control, which allows text input just like a mobile phone.

http://www.kumyoung.net/kym/html/kym_02_search.asp
Above all, the potential for games seems even greater, and it will see the most development and change in the future. The board game market still accounts for the largest share of the overall game market. IPTV, with its good accessibility, seems poised to grow into the best business model for light users to enjoy games without installation.
{{IMG:4}}
[ My LG TV Baduk (Go) game, free games are also available. ]

**2. Disadvantages of Value-added Services**
**1) Low Accessibility**
Currently, the most difficult aspect of using MyLGTv's value-added features is that the menus are too deep, and it's hard to inform users about new features. Besides channels like number 8, which transmits VOD content in an nVOD format during live broadcasts, it would be good to have a channel that advertises value-added services. Also, these value-added features should be able to be registered as shortcuts.
{{IMG:5}}
[ I only found out about the music learning value-added service after deliberately searching for it. ]

**2) Slow Remote Control and Non-intuitive UX**
In addition to complex menus, user accessibility would be further improved if icon-based or widget support were provided.
Recently, Samsung released a TV with a gyro sensor built into the remote control. If IPTV supported this, it could even rival the possibilities of the Wii.
**3) Why not multitasking with live broadcasts?**
Multitasking with live broadcasts also seems necessary. The concept of true interactive broadcasting will emerge when users can enjoy a Go game while watching a Go broadcast.

**3. Development Potential of IPTV Value-added Services**

**1) Convergence with General Video Game Consoles**
I dream of a win-win strategy if IPTV and general video game consoles converge. A large portion of video game console revenue comes from content sales, and combining it with always-online IPTV would make online game implementation and software distribution much easier. What if you could enjoy Mario or Final Fantasy on IPTV? One of IPTV's strengths is also the ability to control children's access. Uncontrolled game playing by children could also be managed.

**2) Various Interactive Services - Shopping, Banking, Medical, Communication**
{{IMG:6}}
[ MyLGTV Shopping Value-added Service ]
As shown above, there are ways to make purchases through some advertising VODs, but they seem limited. You have to select the service directly. The products are not as diverse as Naver Shopping, and I doubted if any user would choose this value-added service just to see this.
I still haven't seen scenarios like shopping for a celebrity's clothes while watching an IPTV drama. (Despite this being a demonstration video always shown when discussing the IPTV market.) The concept of shopping on IPTV is quite old, and despite many discussions and attempts at implementation, the fact that such content and STBs are not yet provided means that IPTV still has a long way to go. Recently, I heard about medical services using IPTV, but given that shopping isn't even properly implemented yet, I'm skeptical. Of course, if desired, VOIP services could be added to IPTV for high-resolution video calls.

Anyway, I hope more IPTV-specific services emerge, and that content providers who earn money from IPTV establish it as a software platform. Next, I plan to post about IPTV's potential as a software platform.

titleEn: Wifi Authentication System for Public Wifi
contentEn:
A while ago, I posted about an ISP's authentication system ([http://blog.naver.com/fstory97/70070221931](http://blog.naver.com/fstory97/70070221931)) for wireless LAN availability, and it seems that there's really talk of a Wi-Fi authentication system ([http://economy.hankooki.com/lpage/industry/200910/e2009102618420270260.htm](http://economy.hankooki.com/lpage/industry/200910/e2009102618420270260.htm)) circulating.
****
**1. Limitations of current unsecured Wi-Fi**
It seems people oppose it, saying it lowers the availability of public Wi-Fi, but I'd rather ask: Is the availability of general Wi-Fi really that good right now? I've used smartphones for quite a long time, and compared to before, when walking around, countless APs are definitely detected. However, there are almost no APs that can be used due to security settings. Occasionally, I gratefully use an open AP, but in those cases, I could easily see that access was granted by typing the AP admin address. While I was grateful, I wondered if I was being too nosy for worrying about the AP owner.

**2. For this, identification of Wi-Fi devices is necessary.**
When cars first appeared, they probably weren't registered. The same was true for firearms. However, as their negative aspects became known, the need arose to control these devices. Since an IP address is fundamentally for routing and not an actual identification ID, it's fair to say that current devices lack identification. That's why complex technologies are used in internet banking for identity verification. If identity verification is required to classify someone as a potential criminal, it could become a similar issue when boarding ships or planes. Currently, there aren't many means to identify criminals. Furthermore, out of fear of these few criminals, APs that could serve as public roads are being thoroughly locked down. If you think a little about why you need to drive a car with a license plate to use public roads, you can easily understand. Wi-Fi authentication is fundamentally about having a means to identify criminals.

**3. As Wi-Fi authentication is implemented by the government, public interest, not profitability, must take precedence.**
Of course, its implementation method must be carefully considered. Wi-Fi authentication for public Wi-Fi must, by all means, be public. Therefore, individual operating costs should be free, like current bank public certificates, and it should be universal enough to be usable with general home APs. Legislation to preserve the profits of certain telecommunication companies must absolutely not happen, and public Wi-Fi abroad should be benchmarked.

**4. The Wi-Fi authentication system needs to evolve in a way that opens up blocked APs.**
Lately, seeing countless blocked APs while walking around, I've felt it's a waste of the public ISM band, and we should move towards a way to fully utilize it. Given the current trend of wireless device proliferation, Wi-Fi bandwidth will soon be overflowing. At that time, FMC (Fixed Mobile Convergence) from Cook&Show will cover entire urban areas, and a seamless environment will be established. For that to happen, a safer network environment is a very important issue, and the Wi-Fi authentication system will be one part of it. Of course, skilled hackers can still spoof MAC addresses, but just as car registration has proven its effectiveness even with the reality of license plate forgery, its effectiveness is expected to remain valid. Identifying and catching ordinary people, not hackers, is already sufficiently possible with current technology, so talking about ordinary people as potential criminals seems a bit too premature.

titleEn: A Thief Entered My Heart
contentEn:
My wedding gifts were stolen. The funny thing is, I didn't even realize they were gone for about 2 or 3 days. I reported it and spoke with the police, but I feel incredibly upset.

What kind of mindset do thieves have to do such things? If it's just about the money, I'd tell them to take it. If they want to live that way, then live that way. By what right do they covet precious items? Do they even know the meaning embedded in that one item? Do they know the sweat and years that went into it? I'm angry at those people who don't know there are things more precious than money in life, and I also feel incredibly sorry for them.

We struggled to get married, not being well-off, and my mother gave me her saved "ssamj 돈" (pocket money) insisting I get my wife a wedding gift. The value of a few hundred dollars isn't what's important. Why, of all days, did I not wear my wedding ring that day? My wife said it was a blessing in disguise that my wedding ring wasn't a diamond, and that a single diamond ring left has no meaning, so she suggested we sell it and get new couple rings.

A while ago, I heard something like this at the Shinwoohoe (Christian fellowship).
That they see many instances of the wicked prospering in the world... The world isn't always bad for the wicked. Many people whose faith is centered on prosperity gospel think that way. "Why do you live so pathetically when you believe in God?" Ultimately, it's often difficult to explain with the human logic of rewarding good and punishing evil.

"Do not follow the counsel of the wicked, but have hope in heaven." This was a verse I had completely forgotten. There were times when I saw the big and small thieves of the world and wondered if I was living foolishly. It might be foolish, but I have to believe, right? Only then will I not regret living a good and righteous life.

I try to hypnotize myself into believing that truly living a pathetic life is living with the heart of the wicked.
What's worse than anything about the wicked, I think, is that by stealing possessions, they steal hearts. Not just their own hearts, but even the hearts of others.

titleEn: [Idea] Desktop Web Editor Smart Finder
contentEn:
**0. Background**
The desktop wallpaper on personal PCs and mobile phones holds a position as important as a browser's start screen.
Many companies create their own wallpapers.
It's hard to find wallpapers that match one's desired taste.

**1. Wallpaper Smart Finder**
- Search by resolution, calendar inclusion, categories like anime, games, illustrations, photos, celebrities, and other tags.
- Company wallpapers (official wallpapers) / User wallpapers (data uploaded by general users)
- User recommendation system

**2. Effects:** Company advertisements, game advertisements, celebrity promotions

**3. Provide Wallpaper Creator (Flex, Silverlight, Java applet, Window App)**
- It could be similar to decorating the main page of a Naver Cafe.
1) Upload source image
2) Select resolution (stretch * shrink * crop)
- Various resolutions from 1920 to 320, or selection by mobile device model.
3) Apply calendar template
4) Enter text
5) Share wallpaper (item factory style)
6) Search wallpaper (Smart Finder)

I thought of this because it's hard to find suitable wallpapers.
Especially those with calendars, many are from before 2009.
I wrote this with the hope that there would be a service that easily finds wallpapers according to one's taste.

titleEn: Why I Blog: No Web 2.0
contentEn:
**1. My Recent Status**
  Lately, I seem to be caught in the compulsion to write and upload something every day. I first dipped my toes into networking with Hitel, and ever since writing a [short story in my second year of middle school](http://blog.naver.com/fstory97/70005184570), I've really enjoyed writing something and showing it to others. I always achieved excellent results in writing contests, and aptitude tests often showed a stronger humanities inclination, like a writer, rather than a computer engineer, albeit by a small margin. However, influenced by Bill Gates, Lee Chan-jin, and my favorite animated films, I dreamed of computers and eventually entered this field. Honestly, I doubt if I would have made a decent living if I had truly pursued writing or art.
 Nevertheless, my desire to write and draw grows stronger with each passing day. I'm captivated by the thought of definitely pursuing writing and art after retirement, but even now, the time I spend writing has increased considerably because of this blog.
 I developed my personal homepage up to version 3.0, and it was at the top of a portal's sub-category. My Cyworld Minihompy even became a 'Best Minihompy,' and there were [times when I felt proud seeing it prominently displayed on the main page](http://blog.naver.com/fstory97/70008662140). How long will I truly stay with this blog? The struggle I faced when moving from Cyworld to a blog was the task of migrating countless data. However, it was regrettable that I couldn't transfer the traces left by many people.
 Even though I say I'm busy, rushed by work, and have no time, when I find myself making time to write something again and again, it feels like an obsession now. Is it because I have a personality that can't stand not speaking my mind? I told my wife something like that when I was pursuing her.
 'Even if you don't love me, I can't stand not telling you...'
 

 Perhaps I like shouting into the void of the internet because I can't shake off a child's loneliness. Of course, I've run a few online communities and met many good people online.
**** 
**2. Question: Is Web 2.0 Really That Meaningful?**
  I've studied Web 2.0 and written a few articles about it, but I wonder if it truly has substance. Human relationships have been studied for thousands of years since the development of human history, and many business applications have been made, but there hasn't been much of a grand revolution. Should we perhaps implement a Human Instrumentality Project? Language emerged, then writing, then printing, then telephones, and eventually the internet, allowing more content to be delivered faster, but are emotional transmission and understanding between people happening any better?
 The term 'collective intelligence' is popular, but perhaps it's creating uniformity of information and thought, and a sense of alienation for those who don't belong? Some people like celebrities, and some people like democracy. Of course, liking celebrities doesn't help much in creating a better world, but even among those who like democracy, there will be people who risk their lives, people who are moderately interested, and people who are more interested in international relief than democracy. The world is not a thrashing threshold at two vectors and a specific value. Various axes exist, and countless value axes exist within an individual, and these value axes constantly interact and change with the outside world. And the same goes for people on the internet.
 Just as there are 'fans' who excessively like celebrities and cause harm, there are also groups that engage in violent protests or abuse the law. Not acknowledging this is akin to the reasons for the collapse of communism, which failed to assume inherent human greed, overly simplified people and systems, and rejected change and development. I believe this is no different for democracy. If we fail to understand and encompass the diverse facets of a society that develops and changes daily, division will deepen, and that division will even tarnish the meaning of democracy. And at the core of that understanding, while society plays a role, the ultimate goals are happiness and the individual. Not every individual likes struggle and achievement. And the most fundamental commonality of this word 'happiness' is that it doesn't happen alone, but through a connection with someone. Even those who pursue democracy seem to be satisfied more by the empathy of having the same thoughts as themselves and being able to do something together, rather than by actually taking central actions to change the world.
 This is actually a mechanism that works even outside of democracy. The happiness of building a family and a doghouse is the same. And the medium for this connection is simply the internet.
 
**3. What's Important is Not the Speed or Number of Connections, But the Meaning of the Connection Itself**
{{IMG:2}}
[Image Source: [http://blog.naver.com/kjmzzang0114?Redirect=Log&logNo=70070201163](http://blog.naver.com/kjmzzang0114?Redirect=Log&logNo=70070201163) ] 

 
 However, looking back, it's true. It's the [idea that no matter how good the medium is, the satisfaction of such happiness is low in an authoritarian family, and at its root is people, not the medium](http://blog.naver.com/fstory97/70005305031). Even if we used carrier pigeons instead of the internet, a connection with a loved one would be happy. The internet is merely an advancement in media that accelerated propagation. Whether it's 1.0 or 2.0, it's the same. Nothing has changed except that the destructive power has increased as the speed has accelerated. Rather, it seems control is becoming increasingly difficult, much like controlling a supercar.
 We now have a medium where thoughts, whether negative or positive, spread rapidly. If so, isn't the way to create a better world and make myself happy, even if it's self-hypnosis, to think many good thoughts and pour good words onto the internet? I believe everyone knows what is good and what makes people feel good.

**4. And... Delusion**
**I've been active on networks for quite a long time, but this digital loneliness doesn't seem to go away.** The expanded network keeps fostering the thought that I am nothing. That's why I keep writing, perhaps to leave some living trace.
 Team Leader Kang once asked me [how long blogs would last](http://www.ebizstory.com/547). What is the difference between a blog and [ancient cave paintings](http://blog.naver.com/hightime7/50005537524)?
{{IMG:3}}
 
  [Image Source: [http://blog.naver.com/hightime7/50005537524](http://blog.naver.com/hightime7/50005537524)]
 
I don't think much has changed. In fact, ancient cave paintings are the predecessor of blogs, and I don't think blogs will disappear [even if the blog service vanishes or its name changes to SNS in the future](http://www.ebizstory.com/548).
 The true meaning of a blog is already embedded in its name: Log.
 Traces of people who have lived. With that, I believe blogs are doing their job quite well.
 Just as I laughed a lot when I saw my father's youthful notes, where everything seemed so serious, I hope, more than anyone, that my children will read my blog.

titleEn: Legend of Dragonia Part 2, Chapter
contentEn:
{{IMG:1}}

When Dagmon opened his eyes again, he was in his quarters. Last night felt like a dream to Dagmon. The wounds he sustained from rolling around yesterday ached. They weren't severe, but they were enough to remind him that yesterday's events were real. A sense of unease crept over him as he wondered why there were people targeting him in the place where Aysia was supposed to be. As he wasn't a major political force in Laodicea and was at least hiding his identity, he couldn't think of any clear reason why he would be targeted within Laodicea.
He also realized that if his identity were revealed, Aysia's safety would be at risk.
"Melchizedek!"
Dagmon urgently called Melchizedek. However, he expected a reply, but no one answered. Dagmon hastily threw on his outer garment and stepped out of the room. As he reached the downstairs stairs, an unwelcome person greeted him from below.
"Hey, Dagmon."
It was Dagmon's second brother, Zacchaeus. Melchizedek was flustered in front of him.
"Greetings, brother. What brings you here?"
Dagmon briefly paid his respects and asked in a displeased tone. His second brother, however, scolded Dagmon instead.
"His Majesty ordered Melchizedek to bring you back as soon as possible so you wouldn't cause trouble, but why do you cause trouble and let news of you reach the palace?!"
Dagmon replied with a troubled expression.
"I don't know what you're talking about. I believe I'm handling my own affairs quite well..."
"If you're doing so well, what are those wounds? Were you attacked by a female spy?"
"What? What are you talking about? A female spy?"
"I have been fully authorized by the head of the intelligence agency, Melchizedek, to handle this matter. I will start by apprehending Aysia, as confirmed by independently gathered intelligence. Be aware of that."
Dagmon was startled when Aysia's name came up and asked again.
"What are you saying? Aysia is a spy?"
"Didn't Melchizedek tell you?"
"Melchizedek! What is this all about?"
Dagmon pressed Melchizedek, who immediately sensed that things were going wrong.
"Well, I was still verifying the authenticity of the information, so it wasn't at a level I could report."
The second prince spoke with an arrogant air.
"For an intelligence chief to be so slow. I, sitting in the palace, have already come with such confirmation."
"As I said, it's still..."
"What is there so much to say? Anyway, as of today, this matter will proceed under my jurisdiction, so be aware of that, and you, my brother, do not act clumsily.
Melchizedek, you are demoted to deputy chief for neglecting your duty to escort Dagmon, and the current deputy chief, Galab, will be appointed as interim chief. Where is the new chief?!"
"Yes! Your Highness!"
Galab, the deputy chief of the intelligence agency who was standing nearby, answered in surprise.
"Immediately apprehend Aysia at the village's quartermaster's post, lead the troops, and search the traveling troupe again. Execute it at once."
"Yes! Understood."
Galab glanced at Melchizedek once, then hastily led the soldiers out.
"Why isn't the deputy chief of intelligence coming along?!"
"Yes! Your Highness!"
Melchizedek was frustrated, but he had no choice but to do as he was told. He hoped Dagmon would plead for him, but Dagmon, seemingly quite flustered by the new situation, just stood rooted to the spot.
Leaving the inn, Melchizedek, along with the deputy chief, mobilized the soldiers and headed towards the traveling troupe. Galab, who had suddenly become chief, approached Melchizedek with a humble expression and spoke.
"Prince Zacchaeus, I mean. For someone like that to be a prince... it's pathetic... For us who faced death together in the Kingdom of Ceres, we will continue to serve you, Chief. No matter how much rank is power, we cannot accept this."
Melchizedek chuckled at his words and said,
"No, no matter what, it's an order from above, so it's best to avoid doing anything that would displease them. I'm from a commoner background, so I have to be careful, but you, on the other hand, have good lineage, don't you?"
The deputy chief replied with a serious face.
"Don't say that. I also initially relied on my family and acted presumptuously, but if I hadn't met you, Chief, and come to my senses, I would have already died in the Kingdom of Ceres. Soldiers speak with skill. My caliber is different from yours, Chief."
Melchizedek looked the young noble, who had just left his youth, up and down and said with a smile.
"You will surely make a good chief."
However, though Melchizedek said that, he once again felt the barrier of social status.
Melchizedek also worried about Aysia and instinctively felt a sense of urgency that he had little time to change the situation.

Bringing all the troupe members to the quartermaster's post was not a major problem. A few gypsy men resisted collectively, but they were no match for the well-armed elite intelligence soldiers. In the process, three gypsy men were seriously injured and taken to the village hospital, but the intelligence agency suffered no minor damage. The quick-witted gypsies, realizing they were no match, quickly became submissive. And when they learned that their destination was not the police station, which handled common criminals, but the quartermaster's post, a military facility, some people shed tears, and one parent even begged for their child's life to be spared.
For them, being taken by the military was clearly a terrifying experience. Melchizedek could say nothing to them, and he was only indignant that the responsibility for this mission lay with Prince Zacchaeus, who was known for his cruelty and foolishness. Upon arriving at the quartermaster's post, the women and children were separated and housed, and among them, Melchizedek spotted Aysia. She, too, was clinging to her companions, looking utterly terrified. Just as Melchizedek was about to approach her, perhaps to say something, a messenger urgently called him. It was Dagmon's summons. Melchizedek entered the central tent of the quartermaster's post. There, instead of Prince Zacchaeus, Dagmon sat alone with a displeased expression.
"What is going on?! Why was the report about Aysia omitted?!"
Dagmon immediately yelled, and Melchizedek tried to answer.
"I suspected it might be information intended to draw Your Highness in. I needed to gather more circumstantial evidence to be sure..."
However, Dagmon reprimanded him again before he could finish.
"What nonsense! Because you handled things that way, the situation has slipped out of my hands!"
Melchizedek felt a surge of anger at those words and wanted to retort, but he swallowed his words. However, Dagmon's harsh criticism continued to pour out. In this situation, it was clear that whatever Melchizedek said would only be counterproductive. Yet, the reason for Dagmon's criticism was not very clear. Melchizedek had done his best, and the source of the information that had leaked to the palace was still unknown.
The information had spread too quickly for the intelligence agency to act, and above all, only Dagmon, Aysia, and Melchizedek knew about their affair, making the information leak path itself highly suspicious.
Dagmon must have known that fact. However, Melchizedek realized, as he had feared, that Dagmon's judgment was being clouded by Aysia. Melchizedek thought that losing Dagmon, who should have been his shield, was an even bigger problem than the foolish second prince.
After a long outburst of anger, Dagmon, seeing that Melchizedek remained silent and continued to listen, finally spoke in a voice that seemed to be suppressing his rage.
"I'm sorry for everything so far. I've been spouting foolish things. I know it's not your fault. But I hope you can understand me, not as a prince, but as a friend. And please do what you can."
Only then, after Dagmon's anger had subsided, did Melchizedek reply.
"Understood. I fully comprehend Your Highness's feelings."
Dagmon patted Melchizedek's shoulder a few times, and Melchizedek somehow felt the current situation was very bitter. Then, as Melchizedek left the central tent, he muttered.
"It's not just understanding. My feelings for Aysia are the same as yours."
Melchizedek recalled Aysia's terrified eyes and shook his head, disliking the feeling. Melchizedek began to interrogate the troupe members one by one again, as ordered by Prince Zacchaeus. However, he expected little gain since it had already been done once. More than that, he was waiting for news from the intelligence agents who were carrying out the orders he had sent to the castle.
But if he outwardly showed disobedience, Prince Zacchaeus would try to take direct command of the work, so he was only pretending to carry out the mission out of concern. The actual investigation of the troupe was entrusted to undercover agents in plain clothes, focusing on those who had external contact with the troupe. He was confident that if there was a spy within the troupe, there would surely be a route for exchanging information with the Kingdom of Ceres.
He was asking perfunctory questions to the frightened troupe members, but the foolish Zacchaeus was merely dozing beside him, and Dagmon, annoyed by the sight, went out of the tent.
Dagmon looked up at the sky once, then down at the ground, and sighed. The sky was only blue, unlike his complicated feelings, and the wind was cool. He decided that he had to reveal his identity as a prince and tell Aysia about the situation so far. But he was afraid. The situation had deteriorated to such an extent, and he was putting her through such hardship; what would she think if he told her the truth now?
Recalling the social gatherings he had attended at the palace made him sick. When they learned he was a prince, many women wanted to catch his eye, and some disgusting nobles wanted to place their unwilling daughters by Dagmon's side.
As a child, he enjoyed it with a sense of pride, tormenting some beautiful young girls until they cried. And because he was intelligent and excelled in his studies, his arrogance grew, and he acted as he pleased. In fact, as a child, he was certainly no better, if not worse, than his older brothers. He later learned that at the time, he was considered the most cunning of the "three little devils" among the common people and nobles who referred to the princes.
So

What brought him to his senses was an old coachman. If he hadn't fallen asleep in the coachman's cart, which supplied milk to the castle, and thus hadn't gone outside the castle walls, and if it hadn't been for that coachman, he would still have been nothing more than a frog in a well. The coachman pretended not to recognize the young prince and mercilessly beat Dagmon, who was rude and disrespectful. For the first time in his life, he was beaten by someone other than his father.
Since the king spent most of his time on the battlefield, the times Dagmon had actually been hit in his life could be counted on one hand. Young Dagmon burst into tears from shock and pain.
However, the coachman was not merely a scary old man. He comforted Dagmon, who was crying in pain, and taught him right from wrong.
The castle was turned upside down, and even soldiers were mobilized to search for the vanished prince, but the coachman, knowing this, did not return him to the castle. Instead, they spent a month together delivering milk. During this time, the young prince directly witnessed the light and shadow of the lives of the common people and the wounds caused by the ongoing war in the Kingdom of Laodicea.
At first, he watched with fear that he might not be able to return to the castle and would have to live like the common people, but young yet intelligent Dagmon fell into a deep shock that was incomparable to the pain of being beaten by the coachman.
A month later, the old coachman, observing the proper etiquette for a prince, returned the young prince to the castle. Upon learning this, the king was furious and, accusing the coachman of insulting the royal family, ordered him to be drawn and quartered and beheaded.
The king's temperament was naturally fiery, but his rage was so immense that everyone was afraid and no one dared to step forward before the king.
However, when young Dagmon stepped forward before the king, observing the etiquette of a subject, everyone could not hide their surprise. The king, still seething with anger, threw a goblet at young Dagmon.
But young Dagmon, bleeding from his head, pleaded with the king for the coachman's life, and the king, impressed by the young prince's remarkably dignified transformation, forgave the old coachman.
After that incident, Dagmon transformed into a thoughtful person who respected others and those of lower status.
During social gatherings, the nobles, knowing that the king's favor was upon Dagmon, tried to keep their daughters close to him. However, Dagmon now found these formal and calculating gatherings stifling rather than enjoyable.
Thereafter, Dagmon often escaped from the castle to enjoy life among the common people and meet the old coachman.
And on the day the coachman was stabbed to death by a drunken soldier, Dagmon, unable to control his rage, killed the soldier and left the castle, beginning to wander.
Whenever his identity as a prince became known, people tended to see his position rather than Dagmon himself. Even those who had been close to him, once they knew he was a prince, either wanted to lean on his position or felt burdened by it and distanced themselves. But Dagmon sincerely wished that his beloved Aysia would see him as Dagmon, the man she loved, not as a prince.

**2. Data from Recommended Search Terms**
If you type Me2day and Twitter into the search bar, a list of active celebrities appears.

First, Twitter is falling behind in terms of numbers, but the real issue is recency. It seems like Me2day celebrities who weren't visible a week ago are appearing again. Recently, they presented the following self-help measure for the disruption caused by Flickr's Me2day closure. It doesn't seem to be applied yet, but it's the integration with N Drive. Also, after enabling widgets on Naver blogs, they held an event like this.
{{IMG:5}}
 
And it has become possible to send posts from Naver blogs to Me2day and Twitter. What does this mean? It means they are expanding interoperability and entry points, which are inherent functions of 2.0. Some people said Me2day has few applications, but currently, there are already 63 applications (excluding web widgets).
[http://me2day.net/me2/app/lastest?page=page_7](http://me2day.net/me2/app/lastest?page=page_7)
Considering the environment of lazy and busy developers in Korea, this is by no means a small number, and applications for the Android platform are already visible.
 
Also, Me2day's features are changing day by day. The conclusion is that Naver's changes are now focused on substance rather than marketing. It seems that its responsiveness to the current domestic user environment is incomparable to Twitter's.
 
Perhaps the reason I can write this is because I use Me2day. If you have more objective data or opinions, please leave a trackback or comment. I think I've also been infected with the Me2day virus...

titleEn: [Share] Search Manipulation is a Criminal
contentEn:
**Naver's Stance on the Criminal Punishment of a Programmer Who Manipulated Real-time Trending Search Rankings**
****

Yesterday, there was a [media report](http://news.naver.com/main/read.nhn?mode=LSD&mid=sec&sid1=001&oid=001&aid=0002897652&) regarding the criminal punishment of a programmer who manipulated Naver's [real-time trending search](http://searchc.naver.com/pw/) rankings to gain illicit profits. Many of you have also shared various opinions about the 'real-time trending search service' through blogs and other channels. To help you understand, we would like to provide an overview of this incident and NHN's position.

First, the program in question is a search result manipulation (abusing) program. The essence of search is to provide users with the answers they are looking for immediately. Abusing refers to the act of using malicious programs or other means to expose specific words at the top of search results for a particular purpose, usually commercial. This fundamentally undermines the basic trust of the internet, and our Supreme Court recently ruled that abusing constitutes a criminal act. (See [related post](http://diary.naver.com/150049031892))

{{IMG:1}} **Abusing Using Infected PCs**

Mr. Seo, who was indicted in this case, created such an abusing program and then uploaded it to an internet bulletin board with the description, 'A program to increase mini-homepage visitors.' However, when users download the program without much thought, malware infects their PCs. The infected user's PC then automatically transmits (inputs search queries) specific words that the hacker had pre-planted on the Naver site. Although smaller in scale, the method is similar to the previous DDoS crisis. (See [related post](http://diary.naver.com/150052750758))

As search services become central to the internet, search query abusing is also increasing. In this regard, Lee Jun-ho, COO overseeing Naver's search technology, stated at a press conference on September 25th, "Abusing is not just a problem for Korea; it's an issue faced by all search engines worldwide. However, because Korea has an excellent internet environment, many more attempts occur here, and consequently, we possess more advanced technology than overseas companies in terms of abuse prevention."

In fact, this incident is one where NHN quickly detected abnormal signs in search queries, traced them back, identified the distribution of malicious programs, and requested an investigation from law enforcement agencies. Of course, it is true that there was concern that this incident might amplify suspicions that "real-time search queries can be manipulated by hackers." However, we judged it more important to respond resolutely because the distribution of malicious programs is not only illegal but also disrupts the internet ecosystem, ultimately harming users. NHN will continue to respond to all illegal abusing attempts with the same principle.

**Search Manipulation is a Criminal Act**

Finally, what I want to say is that search query manipulation is not a 'genius program created by a genius hacker.' As you've seen in this incident, most computer crimes involve tricking multiple users into using a simple program without any suspicion. Of course, Naver may suffer primary damage from such search query manipulation. However, the ultimate victims are all internet users, including myself. This is also why we take a firm stance against internet crimes that exploit the goodwill of users.

Search services, which help us easily obtain desired information free from temporal, spatial, and economic constraints, are useful tools for all of us and have already become an important part of our daily lives. Naver will continue to thoroughly and resolutely block any abusing attempts to repay your unwavering trust.

{{IMG:3}}

mailto:naver_diary@naver.com

**While the anti-Naver camp might say "Typical Naver~" regarding this incident, it seems they overlook the seriousness of personal PC security and the efforts made by service providers to eradicate such issues.**

[Blind Spots of Real-time Search Rankings and the Power of Media](http://blog.naver.com/fstory97?Redirect=Log&logNo=70005116469)
[Naver's Real-time Search Query Problem as Seen in "The Truth About Hwang Woo-suk"](http://blog.naver.com/fstory97?Redirect=Log&logNo=70013144435)
[[DDOS 7.7 Crisis] Why Were 40,000 PCs Idle?](http://blog.naver.com/fstory97?Redirect=Log&logNo=70052336326)
[The Core of the DDoS Attack Incident is Neither the Left Nor Naver.](http://blog.naver.com/fstory97?Redirect=Log&logNo=70052250867)

It seems users still don't understand the concept of "real-time trending search queries" as opposed to just "real-time search queries." They treat it merely as an amusing game or a ranking of public opinion, which is why they parrot questions like "Why was 'Impeachment of Lee Myung-bak' deleted?" And the yellow journalism, inherently irresponsible, writes articles as if it were a foregone conclusion.

What's even more regrettable is that even tech-savvy bloggers and engineers hold such views, which is truly frustrating. Before criticizing someone else's system, if one simply examines the publicly available specifications of the system, it's not that difficult to understand. Isn't it important to objectively examine the subject before criticizing it? Emotional criticism dilutes the basis of an argument and ultimately causes one to stumble.

It seems that societal awareness regarding abusing needs to be established first.

titleEn: [Idea] Efficient Internet Usage Utilizing P2P Servers
contentEn:
1. Title: Efficient Use of the Internet Utilizing P2P Servers
2. Date: June 25, 2009
3. Background
- Services that attract high PVs and a large number of subscribers incur significant costs.
- User PCs or DTEs (modems) remain in an idle state for long periods.
- Currently, P2P is only used for sharing videos, media, and files of specific services.
- All internet resources are identified by a unique address called a URL.
- Most internet resources are not updated frequently.
- Even for resources updated every few seconds to minutes, pages with high PVs require substantial equipment investment.

5. Concept
5.1) Registering Internet Resource Addresses with a P2P Server in a Service System
Resources to be utilized in the system register their unique internet resource addresses with the DNS P2P server.

| URL | [http://blog.naver.com/fstory97/32014231](http://blog.naver.com/fstory97/32014231) |
| --- | --- |
| Original Client | [http://blogreal.naver.com/fstory97/32014231](http://blogreal.naver.com/fstory97/32014231) |
| Reg date | 20090603 13:01:33 |

5.2) User Resource Request
- When a query from the user (browser) input is received, the P2P client on the user's PC connects to the P2P server, rather than going through an address via DNS.
- Alternatively, in a typical scenario, the DNS server directly calls the Naver service domain.
- Then, the [http://blog.naver.com](http://blog.naver.com/) server performs a redirect to the P2P server.

5.3) If User Resource is Not Present on P2P Server
- The address of the Original Client is provided to the user, and the user Client's address is registered in the Client list.

| URL | [http://blog.naver.com/fstory97/32014231](http://blog.naver.com/fstory97/32014231) |
| --- | --- |
| Original Client | [http://blogreal.naver.com/fstory97/32014231](http://blogreal.naver.com/fstory97/32014231) |
| Reg date | 20090603 13:01:33 |
| Client List |  |
| Ip | regDate |
| 10.8.15.3 | 20090603 15:02:44 |

5.4) The user client downloads the content, encrypts the data using a key value issued by DNS, and stores it. (Query and tamper-proofing through encryption)

5.5) Other User's Resource Request (Same as 3.2)

5.6) User Resource Exists on P2P Server
- The address of the Client from the Client list is provided to the user, and the requesting user Client's address is registered in the Client list.

| URL | [http://blog.naver.com/fstory97/32014231](http://blog.naver.com/fstory97/32014231) |
| --- | --- |
| Original Client | [http://blogreal.naver.com/fstory97/32014231](http://blogreal.naver.com/fstory97/32014231) |
| Reg date | 20090603 13:01:33 |
| Client List |  |
| Ip | regDate |
| 10.8.15.3 | 20090603 15:02:44 |
| 10.8.12.1 | 20090603 15:03:01 |

Multiple client addresses are provided instead of just one, to minimize transmission delays in case of changes or no response from a user.

5.7) Resource Download from Another Client by a Client
- When a client receives internet resource addresses from the P2P server, it connects to those addresses to download data. At this time, it checks the transmission status and integrity (tampering) of these resources, generates a report, and sends this report to the P2P server.

5.8) P2P Server Updates Client List Status Information Upon Receiving Report
- Updates the client list based on priority, tampering, or non-responsive clients (cases where the computer is on but the client has been deleted or data lost).

5.9) Resource Update in Service System
- Client List reset, Reg_date change.

5.10) Deleting Accumulated Data on Clients
- Clients set an allowed capacity and only retain data within that capacity. Data not requested by the P2P server for a certain period is requested for deletion permission from the P2P server, and then deleted.

6. Application to DTE Units
- Resources that are always on, consume little power and CPU, and are in standby are modems or routers rather than PCs. These DTEs have a certain level of software processing capability. It is conceivable to implement the above functions by equipping them with a DSP chip or FlashRom to handle these functions, along with inexpensive NAND memory. In this case, QoS can also be guaranteed without degrading PC performance.

7. Value
- Cost reduction through minimal IDC center establishment.
- Increased efficiency of the internet network.
- P2P service as a platform independent of specific services.

titleEn: [Hwang Shin-hye Premian Service
contentEn:
**1. The Development of Personal Consultant Services**
In the 21st century, personal consultant services have become a recent hot topic. In finance, private banking is on the rise, and the concept of a primary care physician is being introduced in medical practice. As industries developed, financial and medical services diversified to maintain competitiveness, and consequently, the range of services individuals could choose from also expanded. While these services were introduced for the benefit of customers, their excessive diversification has led to a situation where, if one doesn't study them, it's almost worse than not having them at all. This is where personalized services, which find optimized services for each individual, emerged. Another reason for their appearance is to solve the problems inherent in the limitations of general-purpose services. I also see this as a result of the growing evidence that customer-centric business behavior is a competitive advantage in increasingly customer-focused industries.

**2. The Era Where IT Also Needs Personalized Services Has Arrived**
However, there's an industry that is becoming increasingly complex and diverse: IT. Just as those who claim to have nothing to do with finance still likely have a paper bankbook, those who say they have no relation to IT are finding that there's hardly anything that isn't an IT device, from cell phones to TVs, cameras, and even cars. While this is a joy for those who are deeply immersed in IT, it's quite perplexing for those who previously lived without much involvement. Yet, the opportunity cost of neglecting IT is quite high. Nowadays, hardly anyone only has a low-interest general savings account at a primary financial institution. The same applies to businesses; there's a vague awareness of IT's potential to improve the corporate environment, but often, they don't know how to go about it. This led to the emergence of IT consulting firms, and more proactive companies even introduce CTOs to align with their corporate strategy. This environment has now begun to reach individuals. A lot of personal key information is being stored on various IT devices, and people are bewildered by new products and technologies that emerge almost daily.
You might see a fascinating new device and think it could be useful for you. However, sometimes you only realize there's a more suitable device after you've fully mastered the first one. This could eventually lead to a digital divide based on digital literacy.

{{IMG:1}}
[Image Source: [http://iptv.commres.org/tag/tv%EC%9D%98-%EB%B3%B8%EC%A7%88/](http://iptv.commres.org/tag/tv%EC%9D%98-%EB%B3%B8%EC%A7%88/)]

Wealthy individuals simply buy new devices or call an employee from an expensive local computer repair shop. Most of what these employees do is reinstall Windows, and sometimes they even commit fraud by replacing parts with cheaper ones. Currently, the best method is to ask for help from someone proficient in IT devices. This is the most effective, but the service is temporary, and there's no guarantee that the proficient person has a lot of time. When I was a student, after assembling dozens of PCs for acquaintances, I sometimes found myself giving up my weekends for PC after-sales service, which was more demanding than the small pocket money I received for assembly.
Now, it's even more complicated than it was then. Even I don't really know which graphics card is better these days. If someone asks me about cameras, even with some knowledge, I have to search for what products have been released in the past few months. I, too, am increasingly reluctant to recommend custom-built PCs. This is because I believe the increasing opportunity cost of service outweighs the decreasing unit price of the devices. Nowadays, I simply recommend laptops. I tell people to take them to the AS center for repairs.

**3. Hwang Shin-hye, the "Computer Beauty," and LG Premian Service!**

My introduction has been long, but it ultimately means that the concept of an IT consultant is also needed for individuals. Seeing the service recently promoted by Powercom, featuring Hwang Shin-hye, known as the "computer beauty," I thought they might be targeting this market. A typical marketing strategy for personalized services is to offer value beyond general-purpose services, often using terms like "premium" and "VIP." LG Powercom's service seems to have adopted this concept.

**4. The Potential of LG Premian Service (Personal IT Consultant)**
Now, let's discuss the potential of this newly launched service.
****
**1) One-stop service for users who don't know where to go**
**** {{IMG:2}}****
[Image Source: stoo.com]

The task of individually searching for AS centers for various IT devices is reduced to a single point of contact for assistance. This would be the best service when you don't even know where to start.

**2) Highly reliable service**
{{IMG:3}}
Personalized services are based on the guarantee of continuous service, so trust is extremely important. While some might call it corporate tyranny, LG's reputation as a large corporation will be effective. If such services expand, local PC repair shops will likely face increasing difficulties. (I'm relieved that those who bother me will decrease. As I always say, **S/W developers are not H/W technicians.**) Also, at least there won't be any unscrupulous parts fraud. If there is, you could sue and potentially extract a larger sum of money.

**3) Women-specific service**
****{{IMG:4}}****
[Image Source: [http://photo.naver.com/view/2006111317320932323](http://photo.naver.com/view/2006111317320932323)]

I've seen many recent advertisements from loan companies targeting women. This is because women, while possessing economic power, often require many services. This is especially effective in IT, where many women claim to be "tech-illiterate." Furthermore, female consultants are very effective for women who are apprehensive about male technicians entering their homes. This seems to be the most commendable aspect of LG's new service. My wife also wanted to call a technician on the weekend for precisely this reason.

**4) Experts to help with difficult installations and settings**
As I've mentioned before, nothing is simple, whether it's installing Windows or a home theater system. If an individual does it, the cables can make it messy and cluttered. This creates a personal assistant who can solve such difficult environments in one go.

**5) Essential security consultant for IT**
Simply installing Eastsoft's ALYac doesn't actually end security concerns. Windows patches need to be applied regularly, and if you're using other software, there's no guarantee that it doesn't have security vulnerabilities. Constantly monitoring these, setting up security configurations during Windows installation, and configuring router security are tasks that even I, who make a living with computers, doubt I'm doing correctly. Furthermore, with the risk of personal information leaks on the web, or if wireless LAN security laws are enacted, settings to avoid violating them, etc., security has become a major issue even for individuals. Perhaps CAPS or AhnLab might jump into this market in the future. (Was my idea that ISP providers should offer security solutions already being put into practice?)

**5. Key Challenges in the Personal IT Consultant Market**
While I've listed the advantages above, are there no problems with such services? I'll discuss the issues I perceive.

**1) Concentration of personal information**
{{IMG:5}}
[Source: Personal Information Protection Act Legislative Notice, Kyunghyang Shinmun 2008.08.12]

Even if it's just device information, that device can contain critical personal information, and the device information itself might be considered personal information. MAC addresses would fall into this category, and they could be matched with a company's personal information and utilized. Of course, due to the Personal Information Protection Act, easy utilization is impossible, but the possibility of legal violations or accidental leaks still exists.

**2) Recommendation of affiliated company devices**
If LG provides the service, they will likely recommend LG products, or even just for ALYac installation, they might recommend devices from their affiliated companies. However, in my case, I prefer iptime for wireless LAN equipment and PC Green, which uses the Kaspersky engine, or the lightweight V3Lite for antivirus. Therefore, portals and various IT device companies will likely accelerate their efforts to partner with such personal IT consultant companies. **(Please, please don't change the start page... Don't change it to Daum when installing Powercom.)** In personal finance, FPs affiliated with specific financial companies also face such situations, and commissions might arise from this. This could limit the user's range of choices. That said, it would be better than choosing completely blindly, and a business model could be built in this way.

**3) Lack of experience, low awareness**
As this service concept has only recently begun, both the companies providing it and the customers will likely face many difficulties. The business model for the performing company will also be a major concern. How much profit can be earned from internet fees alone, and how much will labor costs be, are aspects that need consideration.

**6. The Path the Personal IT Consultant Market Should Take**
**1) Separation of service companies**
It seems necessary to separate the operations currently performed by TPS companies, even if they are subsidiaries. There's a saying that Samsung Electronics' AS Center can provide such good service because it's a different company from Samsung Electronics itself. This is because providing service is directly linked to performance. If not, service would be seen as a cost and expense within the company, leading to reluctance and even more severe recommendations for their own products or affiliated company devices.

**2) Need to consider related laws and systems**
New laws, such as those against unfair trade practices like recommending one's own products or affiliated company devices, might be necessary. However, these laws must be carefully crafted, as they could inadvertently destroy the business model and eliminate the market itself. Furthermore, the issue of personal information remains a key topic.

**3) Related Services, Technology Development**
Various services and new technologies may be required, such as remote PC inspection, repair, on-site visit processes, and SLAs.

**7. Conclusion**
The emergence of new services is always a pleasant thing for consumers, as it means new options become available. I believe this service would have significant competitiveness if it becomes widespread. Individual IT costs will continue to grow, and this market will also expand. What would such a personal IT consultant be called? Perhaps IP (IT Tech. Planner)? It would be confusing with Internet Protocol... so I guess IP won't be used. ^^; No one knows what other services will emerge in the future.

titleEn: How Forest Story Writes Blogs Using Mobile
contentEn:
{{IMG:1}}
 
 To those who want to post despite their busy schedules, I'm sharing how I use my blog, which probably no one is curious about, hoping it might be of some help.
 
**1. Topic Selection
** In my case, interesting topics I find in other people's posts, intriguing newspaper articles, or miscellaneous personal anecdotes like movies, books, travel, things to boast about, or new ideas become the subjects of my posts.
 
** 2. Draft and Body Creation
**I have 30 minutes each for my commute. That time is spent with my Xperia.

{{IMG:2}}

http://shopping.naver.com/detail/detail.nhn?cat_id=36869&nv_mid=5369235659

Brand Sony Ericsson Xperia  
Camera 3.2 megapixels, Communication standard Smartphone, Form Slider, Video call, GPS, Bluetooth, LCD 3.0 inches, Touch Touchscreen, External memory T-Flash (MicroSD), SKT, Xperia, Slider, 3.0-inch, Touchscreen, 65,000 TFT LCD, WVGA, Smartphone, 3G, Video call, GPS, Bluetooth, 3.2 megapixels, External memory, Wi-Fi.
 {{IMG:3}}
 Although DMB doesn't work, I listen to FM radio or MP3s in the background while running a memo program. Then I organize my thoughts using the Xperia's QWERTY keyboard. **(Long live QWERTY!)** It's been about a month since I bought it, and I can now type over 120 words per minute, and I'm even drafting my self-written novel, "The Legend of Dragonia," on this device.
 
 
**3. PC Synchronization**
**{{IMG:4}}****
****
**Most drafts are written on my smartphone like this, and completed articles are synchronized via Outlook within a day or two. I synchronize almost daily for work. Since I can't even think about using data charges, full downloads of recent emails and attachments are always essential.
 
**4. Upload, Edit, Revision**
**** 
**{{IMG:5}}**
[Image Source: [http://grovenor.egloos.com/1919757](http://grovenor.egloos.com/1919757) ]

 After lunch, I have about 40 minutes. I then copy and paste the memo content onto my blog and begin revisions. If I decide a temporary save is needed, I save the post as private and work on it. For about 10 minutes, I search Google and Naver for images related to the post and insert them.
 Then, for another 10 minutes, I adjust the font and title size and refine the content.
 
** 5. Trackback - Completion**
** Reference: [http://ko.wikipedia.org/wiki/%ED%8A%B8%EB%9E%99%EB%B0%B0%EA%B](http://ko.wikipedia.org/wiki/%ED%8A%B8%EB%9E%99%EB%B0%B0%EA%B)
** After the post is uploaded, I find other posts on Naver and Google, or the original posts that inspired me to write, and send trackbacks. Since Naver doesn't allow multiple trackbacks at once, it's quite a tedious task.
 That's how my current blog life operates. I don't think anyone is curious, but that's how it is. Currently, the Xperia is the biggest driving force behind my posts, and this somewhat inconvenient process actually makes me review my writing at least twice. However, if I could wish for more, **the combination of an 800g Viliv S7 and WiBro feels like an ideal setup for me.**
