titleEn: Scarier Google
contentEn:
I recently talked about Apple's terrifying pricing policy due to its 3G phone ([http://blog.naver.com/fstory97/70048575493](http://blog.naver.com/fstory97/70048575493))... but in the bigger picture, I wonder if the truly terrifying company isn't Google.

Whether the next-generation platform is Apple, MS, or Google, there's one ultimate destination: the web.
Cloud computing, which is a hot topic, might actually make the underlying OS less important. No matter how much IE is demonized for being non-standard, web standards are ultimately the trend, and MS is preparing accordingly, expanding its support for standards remarkably with each new version. (In truth, fully supporting web standards requires an enormous amount of effort and hard work.)

Ultimately, assuming web standards are in place and all cross-platform web content, using RIA technology, is indistinguishable from native applications, people won't be torn between Android, Windows, or OS X. They'll simply ponder whether to use Naver or Daum, and Naver and Daum's performance will be determined by how well they run on various browsers.
Beyond that, it's obvious that specialized non-standard features of specific browsers on particular platforms will become market standards, and standards will follow market standards. The day when camera APIs are integrated into the Web is not far off. If a specific mobile browser supports a camera API, you can't call it non-standard, because it's outside the scope that standards currently cover... Then, soon, the standards will incorporate those market standards, and in reality, most standards are not created first, but rather by organizing existing market standards. That's why they call it a 'standards war'.

Computers are generally composed of H/W-OS(Platform)-Application. However, in the case of the web, it's H/W-OS(Platform)-WebBrowser+Plugin(Virtual Machine) - Internet - WebApplication(Service) - Web Legacy System. Cloud computers like web office suites would probably fall into this category.

Let's consider who will win in this situation. For the first generation, the three-tiered structure of H/W-OS-Application included companies like MS, Apple, and IBM.

But let's think about Google. Google's beginning was just WebApplication(Service) - Web Legacy System. As for the Web Legacy system, they're buying power plants and building the world's largest IDCs, so there's nothing more to say. The world's data is already with Google. After all, it was a web company... But then. Suddenly, they started dabbling in OS, and developed a WebBrowser (which honestly performs well). For plugins, there are developers, and for VMs, Oracle's Java... And for the Internet, Google is even trying to buy 700Mhz wireless spectrum. ㅡㅡ; Looking at it that way, they already possess most of the foundation for next-generation systems. The core of the Web Application market, the search market, is monopolized! (What is this! Isn't the game already over? They're already at a Big Brother level more terrifying than MS.)
The parts they haven't covered are clearly segmented markets, and since they are essential layers, fierce competition isn't necessarily required.

I thought Apple was amazing, but when comparing Google, MS, and Apple, Apple has the smallest coverage. Although it covers H/W, as seen in the relationship between IBM and MS, it's not a particularly good market. MS, on the other hand, seems to be catching up with its inherent strength in areas it previously couldn't cover. The feel of MS's search engine BING ([http://www.bing.com/](http://www.bing.com/)) is quite good. Giving up on things like MSN was a really smart move. Their attempt to approach immersive reality gaming with X-BOX is also good, differentiating them from Google. In terms of next-gen UI, they might have even scored a point over Apple this time. (Come to think of it, it's similar to NHN, which combines information [Naver] and entertainment [Hangame].) However, compared to Google's cosmic plans (like building unpowered IDC centers using abandoned container ships in the ocean, launching satellites, and buying fighter jets...), they still have a long way to go.

From a user's perspective, this war is good no matter who wins, but as someone in this industry, I need to be careful not to get caught in the crossfire (literally, 'watch out for the shrimp's back').
Domestic users were enthusiastic about features like satellite view, Street View, and panorama in Naver and Daum's map services, but Google is already flying around in 3D, and has even ventured into the underwater world, space, and the moon. They've even announced a 3D API for the web ([http://www.zdnet.co.kr/ArticleView.asp?artice_id=20090608115600](http://www.zdnet.co.kr/ArticleView.asp?artice_id=20090608115600)), already trying to create an environment where 3D MMORPGs can run. What's even more surprising is that this is just one of Google's many changes, and if a Korean company tried to do this, they'd have to stake the company's survival on it. In Daum's case, the reaction was good, but it seems they're struggling with costs because they couldn't connect it to a business model that increases local searches.
Google, you guys are truly amazing! Or should I say, it's the power of scale and money? Everything seems big in America. I wonder how far Google's world domination will continue.

So, I guess Korea should just stick to application development and laying down networks... ㅡㅡ;

titleEn: The Truly Frightening Apple
contentEn:
[http://www.zdnet.co.kr/ArticleView.asp?artice_id=20090609102532]
What's truly scary about foreign companies isn't just when they release cool features, but when well-known companies abroad execute aggressive marketing. Apple, which is about to launch, took quite a long time to come out but didn't introduce new features. However, it seems to have pulled out a card even scarier than new features: 'price.' The price, which makes one wonder how much profit they'll make selling that device, directly emulates how mobile carriers used to slash phone prices. Did they learn from Korean mobile carriers? At least their goal isn't to continuously extract money from consumers' wallets, but rather to profit from content distribution through platform dominance. So, from a user's perspective, it's simply great to buy a good product cheaply... Apple's strategy is now clearly felt.

Unconditional platform dominance.
Perhaps they had a lot of pent-up frustration with Windows in the PC market.

Their opponents here are not LG Electronics or Samsung Electronics, who developed devices. Ultimately, it can only be MS and Google.

In fact, there's nothing more annoying to technically tune than a mobile phone (the crazy act of changing XML and HTML is enough for developers), and because there's a clear user demand for highly polished products, the iPhone's highly refined UI and a platform where the UI can be changed even without development knowledge are naturally welcomed.

Is it like a fish in water? The problem is, if Apple lacks one thing compared to MS and Google, it's a shortage of supporting applications in PC or web environments. Apple doesn't have Gmail or MS-Office. I believe Apple is well aware of this point. And precisely because they know this weakness, they are launching such a terrifying offensive. Moreover, since openness is the trend, whether it's Gmail or MS-Office, with Open APIs and Open Documents, Apple might not have much to fear.

It feels a bit bittersweet that Apple, which has maintained the most closed platform policy, seems to be benefiting from other platforms opening up. However, one must admit that Jobs is a genius who makes great products, reads the market incredibly well, and has top-notch marketing skills, making people feel they need something even when they don't. So, we have to acknowledge that.

Should I splurge on an Apple phone next? Somehow, Apple has a certain "swag." I'm not interested in luxury bags, but perhaps I endure inconvenience for that feeling. Digital luxury, Apple. There's no better way to describe it. In a good way, it's a well-made, excellent luxury item. In a bad way, it's "doenjang." Anyway, that "doenjang" has lowered its price. So. Now I hope Apple opens up a bit more. Wasn't Apple the one who benefited most from the technology of OpenAPI and Open-Doc? Don't keep the multi-touch patent so tightly wrapped up... Please, open up.

titleEn: [Software Engineering] Software Size Estimation
contentEn:
Topic: Software Size Estimation
Author: Forest Story ([http://blog.naver.com/fstory97](http://blog.naver.com/fstory97))
Related Topic: FP, COCOMO, IFPUGA-FPA
Attached File: A Study on the Improvement System for Software Project Cost Standards (Ministry of Information and Communication, Korea Software Industry Association)
Related url: [http://blog.naver.com/khc9981/50033908666](http://blog.naver.com/khc9981/50033908666) 
[http://wrice.egloos.com/4843301](http://wrice.egloos.com/4843301) 
[http://blog.naver.com/yasa68/130001918338](http://blog.naver.com/yasa68/130001918338) 
[http://selab.smu.ac.kr/bbs/zboard.php?id=freeboard&no=100](http://selab.smu.ac.kr/bbs/zboard.php?id=freeboard&no=100)
[http://blog.paran.com/kyjongdari/25410265](http://blog.paran.com/kyjongdari/25410265)
 
 
**1. Concept of Software Size Estimation**
 - Due to characteristics such as software's invisibility and changeability, it is difficult to predict the resources to be invested in development. This technique, as defined by ISO 14143-1, involves predicting and understanding the quantitative and qualitative size of software to estimate and manage the resources, costs, and personnel required. It is divided into methods that measure input effort and methods based on deliverables. Methods based on deliverables include FP, which considers both quantitative and qualitative levels, and COCOMO, which is based on LOC (Lines of Code) and focuses on quantitative levels.
** a. Difficulties in Software Size Estimation**
   - Invisibility of software
   - Many human-dependent factors
   - Strong dependency on development technology and environment
   - Emergence of new technologies
   - Low precision
** b. Classification of Software Size Estimation Methods**
     {{IMG:1}}
 
** c. IFPUG** (International Function Point User Group: The world's largest user group for FP methods, headquartered in the US)
   
**2. Comparison of FP and COCOMO**

| Item | COCOMO | FP |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Characteristics | LOC-based. Coefficient application | Considers function, complexity, and weight by task |
| Estimation Method | Bottom-up | Mathematical method |
| Advantages | Relatively simple | Realistic |
| Disadvantages | Unrealistic | Ambiguous application of complexity and weight |

 - COCOMO evolved into COCOMO II with applied coefficients.
** - FP Element Diagram**
 {{IMG:2}}
**3. Comparison of FP Simplified Method and Regular Method**
** a. Comparison by Classification**

| Classification | Regular Method | Simplified Method |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Primary Purpose | Detailed function point measurement | Rough estimation |
| Measurement Items | Data functions, DET/RET Transaction functions, DET/FTR | Data functions Transaction functions |
| Complexity Application | Complexity applied by function | Average complexity |
| Advantages | Accurate SW size measurement and diverse application experience, DB accumulation and reusability possible | Speed of SW size measurement and minimization of estimation costs |
| Disadvantages | Difficult to apply in early stages of project | Limited data utilization |
| Application Timing | After analysis/design phase for SW development/maintenance size estimation | Applicable during budget planning/proposal phase, insufficient estimation data, and verification of calculated function points |

**** 
**b. Comparison of Estimation Methods**
{{IMG:3}}
    - The only difference is in determining the complexity weight.
 
**c. Function Point Analysis (FPA)**: Analysis of the number of functions and weights for ILF, EIF, EI, EO, EQ.
 - Measures the functions required by the user.
 - Measures the size of software development and maintenance regardless of implementation technology.
 - A normalization factor for software comparison.
 
**d. Function Point Measurement Procedure**
** **
**e. FP Simplified Method Example**
 - Problem: Given the number of functions and average complexity weights, calculate the adjusted development function points AFP (DFP) using the simplified method.

| **Category** | **Number of Functions** | **Average Complexity Weight** | col4 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Data | ILF | 3 | 7.4 |
| EIF | 1 | 5.5 | |
| Transaction | EI | 3 | 4.3 |
| EO | 1 | 5.4 | |
| EQ | 2 | 3.8 | |

 
1) Calculate the average score per function
  - Formula: Average score per function = Number of functions * Average complexity weight
   IFL Function Average Score (22.2) = 3 * 7.4
   EIF Function Average Score (5.5) = 1 * 5.5
   EI Function Average Score (12.9) = 3 * 4.3
   EI Function Average Score (5.4) = 1 * 5.4
   EO Function Average Score (7.6) = 2 * 3.8
2) Calculate Unadjusted Function Points (UFP)
 Sum of average function scores (53.6) = 22.2 + 5.5 + 12.9 + 5.4 + 7.6
3) Calculate Degree of Influence (TDI)
  Score 0-5 for 14 items based on system characteristics. Assuming all are 2.5 as no TDI is given.
  Sum of scores for 14 items = 2.5 * 14 = 35 = Degree of Influence (TDI)
4) Calculate Value Adjustment Factor (VAF)
  - Formula: VAF = (0.01 * TDI) + 0.65
    VAF = (0.01 * 35) + 0.65 = 1
 5) Calculate Adjusted Development Function Points
  - Formula: AFP (DFP) = UFP * VAF
    UFP (53.6) * VAF (1) = AFP (DFP) = 53.6
 *** Precautions for Simplified Method Estimation**
   - Importance of determining average complexity weights appropriate for the application timing and system environment: Utilize certified standard indicators.
   - When applying the degree of influence based on system characteristics, consider complexity focusing on key factors and apply correction coefficients.
   - If identifying data/transaction function counts is difficult, utilize previously accumulated FP calculation results.
**** 
**4. FP Issues by Phase**

| **Phase** | **Issue** | **Activity** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Measurement Preparation | Clarify Scope/Boundary | Understand measurement purpose, set measurement scope and boundary, review results |
| Acknowledge Measurer Skill Differences | FP understanding (practical case-based training), standardization work, simulation | |
| Participation of Field Personnel | Consensus building (workshops, theoretical/practical training), concurrent requirements definition activities | |
| Participation of Expert Personnel | Education consulting by experts, Q&A, development of alternative elements | |
| Measurement Process | Difficulty of Measurement Itself | EO/EQ functions, FTR/RET complexity, etc., case-based, apply average values |
| Measurement Work Productivity | If dependent on manual work, productivity decreases, introduce measurement tools, customization | |
| Differences by System Environment | Subtle differences in measurement methods for CS/web environments, importance of standardization | |
| Measurement Results | Knowledge Management Plan | Document measurement process/results, develop methodology for data accumulation and reuse |
| Impart Objectivity to Measurement Results | Review measurement results, compare with paid experience DB and LOC, correction | |
| Linkage with Contracts | Calculate contract amount based on FP, simulation, prove objectivity | |

 
**5. Future Outlook for Software Size Estimation**
** a. Emergence of New Software Prediction Models**
  - Neural network models: Modeling for quantitative and non-quantitative processing
  - Case-based models: Based on past similar experiences
** b. Focus on Object-Oriented and Component-Based Prediction Methods**
  - LOC methods are fading, FP methods are an alternative.
** c. Cost Estimation Prediction for External Program Factors**
  - Development environment, programmer quality, product complexity, reliability, available time, technical level, etc.

titleEn: [Software Engineering] Open Software
contentEn:
Topic: Open Source Software
Author: Forest Story ([http://blog.naver.com/fstory97](http://blog.naver.com/fstory97))
Date: June 3, 2009
Reference URL: [http://wiki.kldp.org/wiki.php/OpenSourceLicenseGuide](http://wiki.kldp.org/wiki.php/OpenSourceLicenseGuide)
[http://blog.naver.com/jinofstar?Redirect=Log&logNo=130026514651](http://blog.naver.com/jinofstar?Redirect=Log&logNo=130026514651)
[http://blog.naver.com/asura71?Redirect=Log&logNo=30022025938](http://blog.naver.com/asura71?Redirect=Log&logNo=30022025938)
[http://blog.naver.com/jungman3?Redirect=Log&logNo=10034197048](http://blog.naver.com/jungman3?Redirect=Log&logNo=10034197048)
[http://www.bywoong.com/1227](http://www.bywoong.com/1227)
 
**1. Concept of Open Source Software**
 - Software characterized by free use, reproduction, distribution, and modification, with its source code publicly available. It doesn't mean "free of charge" but rather "non-proprietary," meaning it can be used for commercialization.
** a. 10 Open Source Conditions Defined by OSI**

| Free Redistribution | No royalties or sales fees |
| --- | --- |
| Source Code | - The program must include source code, and can be distributed in compiled form - Obscure source code cannot be used |
| Derived Works | Modification and derived works are possible, distributed under the same conditions as the original software's license |
| Integrity of Source Code | - Restrict distribution of modified source code only when allowing distribution of patch files - Create different versions, different names through modification and derived works |
| Equality of Individuals or Groups | - No discrimination against any individual or group |
| Equality for Fields of Endeavor | - No restrictions on use in specific fields |
| License Distribution | - The license is valid wherever the program is redistributed - No need for additional license issuance |
| License Must Not Be Specific to a Product | - The license applies to the entire program - Even partial use requires compliance with the license |
| License Must Not Restrict Other Software | No restrictions on other software distributed with it |
| License Must Be Technology-Neutral | Does not restrict technology or interface style |

** b. Comparison with Similar Concepts**

| Name | Concept | Scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Free Software (Freeware) | - Concept created by Richard Stallman and FSF (Free Software Foundation) - A subset of Open Source - Did not include whether commercial use was allowed - Some freeware is limited to users (in this case, it is not included in the scope of open source software) | Software, Source |
| Shareware | - A form of computer software marketing - Limited in usage period or functionality - Similar term to Trial Version | Software |
| Open API | - A web interface to access free services existing on the web | Web Service |

**** 
**2. Open Source Software Licenses**
 a. Characteristics of Open Source Licenses
  - Common Compliance Requirements

| Item | Content | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Maintain Copyright Notice | Do not modify or change copyright-related information | Developer information at the top of the source code |
| Prevent Product Name Duplication | - Do not use identical product names or service names - Often registered as trademarks | Name of open source software |
| Combining Different Licenses | - When combining licenses, check for compatibility and uncertainty | GPL3.0 + Apache License 2.0 possible. MPL (only part specified as MPL) and GPL (entirely specified as GPL) combination is not possible |

  - License-specific Compliance Requirements

| Item | Content | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Explicitly State Usage | Explicitly indicate the use of the open source software | List used open source in the manual |
| Source Code Disclosure | If there are modifications or additions, the source code must also be disclosed | GPL |
| Patents | If a specific technology is protected by a patent, permission from the patent holder is required | New open source licenses include patent-related clauses |

 
** b. Comparison of Major Licenses**

| **Type** | **Supporting Organization** | **Free Use** | **Distribution Allowed** | **Source Acquisition** | **Source Modification** | **Obligation to Disclose Derivative Works** | **Proprietary SW Combination** | **Features** | **Products** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **GPL** | FSF | O | O | O | O | O | X | Not for commercial use | Linux, MySQL |
| **LGPL** | FSF | O | O | O | O | O | O | Relaxed GPL, no need to disclose source code of programs using linking. | GTK+, Smart Editor |
| **BSD** | University of Berkeley | O | O | O | O | X | O | No obligation to disclose source code | FreeBSD, Cubrid |
| **Apache** | ASF | O | O | O | O | X | O | Difficult to combine with GPL2.0 due to patent clauses | Tomcat, Neptune |
| **MPL** | Mozilla | O | O | O | O | O | O | No need to disclose content not in the original source (clearer than GPL) | Firefox |

 
**3. Major Open Source Issues**
 a. Source Code Disclosure
  - Source code must be disclosed for derivative works of software, but it is difficult to mechanically distinguish between derivative works and mere aggregations.
  : Linux Kernel: Dynamic kernel modules (Loadable Kernel Modules) also operate by linking with the GPL Linux kernel, but an exception is recognized.
  : Java Platform Case: The JVM of the GNU Classpath project is GPL, but other Java Applications linked to and operating on that JVM are recognized as exceptions.
** b. Patent Rights**

| Category | Patent Owner | Rights |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Licensor | Copyright Owner | - Patent rights are treated separately from open source licenses - Royalties can be collected if used in proprietary licensed S/W |
| Licensee | User | - No issue if patent rights are not asserted, but if asserted, the open source license expires, and royalties can be calculated |
| Third Party | Third Party | - Distribution is not possible if the owner does not allow a royalty-free patent license |

** c. Dual Licensing**
  - Using multiple licenses: For commercial use and open source community collaboration.
**4. Open Source License Management/Utilization Strategies in Companies**
 a. Advantages of Adopting Open Source Software

| Advantage | Value | Remarks |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Low Entry Cost | Low cost | Free download and source code modification/redistribution on the web |
| Fast, Flexible Development | Fast and flexible response to latest technologies | Share latest technical information, problems, and solutions |
| Open Formats & Protocols | Interoperability | Efforts to resolve incompatibility between commercial programs |
| Reliability & Stability | Reliability, stability | Participation of many excellent developers |
| Networking | Support for diverse and powerful networking features | Open Source Networking Solution compatible with commercial programs |

** b. Open Source Utilization Process**

| Stage | Activity | Considerations |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Planning | Determine open source utilization scope, decide disclosure for each component | Value obtained from open source utilization, intellectual property rights protection, potential for patent infringement lawsuits |
| Implementation | Actual implementation activities | Be careful not to include company's intellectual property rights |
| Verification | Source code verification | Parts where developers failed to verify licenses during implementation |
| Productization | Reflect in actual product | Confirm source code disclosure, explicit statement of usage |

**5. Revised GPL 3.0 (June 29, 2007)
a. Background**
   - Need to reflect legal systems of various countries
   - Consideration of patent rights
   - Issues with compatible licenses
   - Increase in new technologies
**a. Tivoization and DRM**
   - Tivo, which used GPL, released its source code but did not provide installation information, causing users to be unable to operate it normally.
   - In 3.0, a provision for including installation information was added, and the title of the DRM-related provision was changed to "Digital Restrictions Management."
   - DRM that includes programs covered by GPL3.0 does not receive legal protection.
**b. Treatment of Patent Rights**
   - When a patent holder distributes under GPL, they cannot assert patents against users of that software.
   - Third-party patents can only be distributed under GPL if the patent holder provides a free license to GPL users.
**c. License Compatibility: Apache, Affero GPL**
   - When the licenses of the combined codes conflict with each other
    => If code A under MPL conditions and code B under GPL conditions are combined, GPL requires GPL to be applied to 'A+B', while MPL requires the A portion to remain under MPL.
     Therefore, 'A+B' that satisfies the requirements of both licenses cannot be developed.

titleEn: [Software Engineering] Leader Document
contentEn:
**1. Principles of Software Engineering**
A systematic **engineering approach** to **development, operation, maintenance, and retirement** by utilizing **Process, Tool, and Method** to resolve the **software crisis** where software productivity decreases and quality deteriorates due to the **enlargement and complexity** of software.
 
**2. SDLC**
A **software development strategy** that integrates **processes, methods, tools, and general software engineering process phases** to **visualize and systematize the entire development process** of **feasibility study, requirements analysis, design, development, testing, maintenance, and retirement**, which can assist in **project cost estimation, planning, standardization of terminology, and project management**.
 
**3. Types of Prototypes**
A rough prototype created to eliminate the problem of **requirements uncertainty** is called a prototype. It is divided into an **experimental prototype** to confirm the necessity of a certain function and an **evolutionary prototype** to gradually increase the completeness of development. Problems with prototypes include **customers being satisfied with the prototype** or developers **lowering quality because it's 'just a prototype'**.
 
**4. Comparison of Incremental and Evolutionary Development Methods**
Methodologies through **iteration** include incremental and evolutionary methods. The **incremental method** proceeds by **breaking down into increments** when **requirements are clear**, while the **evolutionary method**, when **requirements are unclear**, involves **developing core technologies first and then adding details** to **flesh out the requirements**.
 
**5. 4 Phases of RUP and Activities per Phase**
RUP, an iterative and incremental methodology, encompasses almost all techniques and deliverables such as **use cases, architecture, patterns, and components**, making its **methodological features very rich**. It has a **2-dimensional process structure**, where the **horizontal axis represents change over time, consisting of 4 dynamic phases**: the **Inception phase** which involves overall understanding of requirements and defining development scope, the **Elaboration phase** for requirements specification and prototype implementation, the **Construction phase** for actual design and implementation, and the **Transition phase** for Best Test, performance testing, and user training. The **vertical axis represents core workflows, which are logical groupings of activities**. From a static perspective, this is expressed through process components, activities, workflows, artifacts, and workers. Each phase has key activities, but these activities do not strictly end within their phase; they can also proceed in other phases. It also has drawbacks such as **lack of adequate guidance for conflicts in best practices** and **implementation not starting until system analysis and design are complete**.
 
**6. CBD / SOA**
Component-based development, which is not language-dependent (OOP) and performs independent functions through **interfaces** as **replaceable parts**, has been materialized through **EJB, COM+**, etc., contributing to **maximizing reusability**. The components of a component consist of a **component made up of context and interface**, a **container** that manages the creation and destruction of components, and an **application server** that supports load balancing, multiprocessing, and transactions. However, as **platform-specific compatibility** was not secured and **business-side reusability** declined, **service-oriented web-based SOA** emerged. SOA consists of **service consumers, service providers, and service registries**, and utilizes technologies such as **XML, UDDI, and SOAP**.
 
**7. Module / Component**
**A module refers to a software design unit that minimizes coupling and maximizes cohesion to facilitate maintenance and development**. A component refers to a **specific type of unit module that performs functions through interfaces bound at runtime, is packaged, specified, deployable, and can be assembled with other components**.
 
**8. Characteristics and Advantages of Component Development**
**Characteristics of components** include 1) **implementation** in a completed state for runtime binding, 2) **specification** describing the component's purpose, type, technical standards, and interface information, 3) **standards** for developing reusable and replaceable components, 4) **packaging** that provides documentation and code together, and 5) **deployment** as an independent unit. Due to these characteristics, it is not language-dependent and can increase reusability through assembly. Component-based development is broadly divided into **Component Development Process (CD) and Component-Based Application Software Development Process (CBD)**. **Component Development (CD)** is [Domain Analysis -> Domain Design -> Component Extraction -> Component Design -> Component Implementation -> Component Certification -> Configuration Management (Repository)]. Component-Based Application Software Development (CBD) is [Requirements Definition -> Domain Analysis -> Component (Repository) Search/Base Design -> Component Assembly -> Application Completion].
 
**9. Black Box Test, White Box Test**
From an SDLC perspective, **White Box Testing**, primarily used for **unit testing** corresponding to **detailed design**, includes **basis path testing, loop testing, and control structure testing**, and is mainly used by developers for **verification** to test the basic operation of functions. **Black Box Testing**, primarily used for **integration testing** corresponding to **architecture design**, includes **equivalence partitioning, boundary value analysis, graph analysis, and empirical methods**, and is mainly used by professional testers for **validation**, a process of testing whether requirements are met.
 
**10. Test Case**
To improve test quality, the most important aspect from an ROI perspective is the selection of Test Cases. From the **Test Basis**, **Test Cases** are extracted to create a **Test Scenario** consisting of multiple consecutive Test Cases, and a corresponding **Test Oracle (expected result)** is created to execute the Test Scenario and verify the Test Cases. The quality of Test Cases can be **evaluated** through **debugging** or **mutation testing**, and it is important to manage Test Cases by creating a **Repository**, utilizing them as corporate knowledge, and **automating** them to increase efficiency.
 
**11. Regression Test**
It is a **test to confirm that there are no issues with the system's requirements and functions when changes, additions, or deletions are made** to the system. Since it must be executed with every change, it requires **repeated impact analysis** and is characterized by **high costs as the entire suite must be run each time**. To reduce these costs, **automation** is crucial.
 
**12. Risk-Based Test, Exploratory Test**
**Risk-Based Testing** is a **priority-based test** that involves evaluating possibility and impact in advance, **analyzing risks**, and then testing accordingly. **Exploratory Test** is a **priority-based test** conducted by test experts or users, focusing on **well-known vulnerabilities and 'bad smells'**.
 
**13. Sandwich Integration Method in Incremental Integration**
For integration, there are **bottom-up integration using Drivers** and **top-down integration using Stubs**. The sandwich integration method **uses both Drivers and Stubs to prioritize the integration of core functionalities**, with the **advantage of being able to verify core functionalities first**.

titleEn: [Software Engineering] Object-Oriented
contentEn:
**Topic:** Object-Oriented
**Author:** Forest Story ([http://blog.naver.com/fstory97](http://blog.naver.com/fstory97))
**Date:** May 29, 2009
**Related TOPIC:** Object Modeling, Method (Overloading/Overriding), JAVA Interface, OR-Mapping
**Reference URLs:** [http://bronto.egloos.com/2077473](http://bronto.egloos.com/2077473)
[http://kjhofone.tistory.com/entry/자바의-인터페이스interface](http://kjhofone.tistory.com/entry/%EC%9E%90%EB%B0%94%EC%9D%98-%EC%9D%B8%ED%84%B0%ED%8E%98%EC%9D%B4%EC%8A%A4interface)
[http://blog.naver.com/ahnsh0830?Redirect=Log&logNo=110044349110](http://blog.naver.com/ahnsh0830?Redirect=Log&logNo=110044349110)
[http://blog.naver.com/oconer?Redirect=Log&logNo=29810772](http://blog.naver.com/oconer?Redirect=Log&logNo=29810772)
**Attached File:** OR-mapping data (Inforever)
 
**1. What is Object-Oriented?**
  A development methodology that implements systems by modeling real-world entities (Entity) around the concept of an object (Object) that combines state (Attribute) and behavior (Method).
** a. Value of Object-Oriented Programming**
  - Extensibility and reusability using inheritance and polymorphism
  - Supports real-world objects at a conceptual level
**** 
**2. Basic Concepts of Object-Oriented Programming**
**  a. Components of Object-Oriented Programming**

| Component | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Object | Represents concepts existing in the real world with data and functions |
| Message | Method of communication between objects; accesses object data by calling functions of external objects |
| Class | A template for objects with the same kind and characteristics |
| Instance | An actual object derived from a class |

**  b. Key Concepts of Object-Oriented Programming**

| **Concept** | **Meaning** | **Implementation** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Encapsulation | Data and functions bundled into one box | Collection of attributes and methods |
| Information Hiding | Controls arbitrary changes to data by accessing it only through specific functions | Public Method |
| Polymorphism | The same function name is used for multiple purposes | Overloading: Multiple method definitions; Overriding: Redefining methods in a subclass |
| Inheritance | Inheriting common characteristics from a superclass through a hierarchical structure | Single Inheritance: Supported by JAVA (more explicit); Multiple Inheritance: Supported by C++ (higher extensibility) |

 
**3. Object Modeling Process**

| Phase | Activity | Details |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Planning | Define scope, business requirements | Resource evaluation, phased strategic planning |
| Analysis | Object (Static) Modeling | Define objects/classes |
| Dynamic Modeling | Analyze activities and flow between objects | |
| Functional Modeling | Express functional processing of identified objects | |
| Design | System Architecture Design | Architecture design based on problem domain analysis |
| Detailed Object Modeling | Elaborate conceptual modeling (object, dynamic, functional) | |
| | Derive classes, define operations, identify relationships between objects | |
| Implementation | Programming | Implement class variables, methods, class interfaces |
| Testing | Unit Test | White Box Test |
| Integration Test | Black Box Test | |

 
**4. Concept of Java Interface**
 - A class composed only of abstract methods (a class that requires concrete methods to be instantiated) and final variables (static variables that cannot be changed).
** a. Usage**
   1. When similarity between unrelated classes needs to be expressed
   2. When declaring methods that are desired to be commonly implemented
   3. When only the programming interface should be shown while the class is hidden
** b. Differences from Class Inheritance**
   - Multiple interfaces can be applied to a single class
   - Inherits only constants
   - Independent of class hierarchy
** c. Syntax**
  access_modifier class [extends ClassName] implements InterfaceList {
   // Implement methods declared in the interface
   }
 
**5. Comparison with CBD**

| **Item** | **Object-Oriented Programming** | **CBD** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Development Pattern | - Developers develop all programs in detail - Lack of standards - White Box level framework | - Focus on combining provided components with business tasks - Provides standard interfaces |
| Skill Level | - Requires advanced object-oriented developers - Module production technology level | - Component experts and component assembly/application developers work together - Developers understand and assemble components |
| Development Process | - Traditional software SDLC - No iteration (Literation) by phase | - Iterative process by stage - Mini-projects possible (Literation) |
| Interoperability | - Low interoperability between heterogeneous systems - Potential for development in specific-purpose environments | - Can connect different objects and components to create a single large object - Applies standardized technologies |

 
**6. OR-Mapping (Object-Relational Mapping)**
 - Mapping between classes in OO programming and RDBMS tables used as data storage.
** a. Mapping between OOP Code and RDBMS**

| **OOP Code** | **Mapping Content** | **Database** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| class | Real-world entity | table |
| attribute | Attribute value of an entity | column |
| Class Relationship | Relationship between entities | Relational Relationship |

 
**  b. Mapping OOP and RDBMS Relations**

**1. Concept of Software Architecture**
** a. Definition of Architecture (IEEE1471)**
   - Architecture: The fundamental organization of a system embodied in its components, their relationships to each other and to the environment, and the principles guiding its design and evolution.
** b. Key Concepts of Architecture **

| **Concept** | **Content** | **Example** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Domain | Architecture exists for specific scopes | Software Architecture, System Architecture, Enterprise Architecture, Hardware Architecture |
| Structure | Structural characteristics between elements | Subsystems, Processes, Libraries, Databases, Computing Nodes, Legacy Systems, Products |
| Operation | Defines interactions between structural elements | UML Sequence Diagram |
| Focus on Key Elements | Abstract the system to focus on key elements, omitting or simplifying non-key elements | Requirements, Risk Analysis, Executable Software Implementation |
| Stakeholder Requirements | Decisions on conflicting requirements among stakeholders | End-users demand reliability, availability, security; marketers demand competitive features, cost |
| Theory for Decisions | Provides theoretical basis for decisions | Used when architecture is reviewed and when architects make decisions |
| Style | Similarities derived from systems sharing similar domains | Distributed Style, Pipe-and-Filter Style, Data-Centric Style, Rule-Based Style |
| Team Structure | Defines grouping of related elements covering a given area | Defines software development team structure according to architecture |

**** 
**  2. Relationship between Design Patterns and Architecture**
    a. Design Patterns as a Style of Software Architecture
      - Design patterns are a subset of software architecture that define the structure and operation of software.
          Architecture > Software Architecture > Design Pattern   
      - Value: Solutions to recurring similar problems
      - Design patterns are primarily software architecture used in the detailed design phase.
      b. Key Design Patterns

**3. Architecture in Practice**
** a. IEEE1471**
   - Value: An international standard defining terms and concepts related to architecture.
 
 
Source: [http://www.ibm.com/developerworks/rational/library/nov06/ferm/](http://www.ibm.com/developerworks/rational/library/nov06/ferm/)
 
  - Architectural Description Creation Process
 
              {{IMG:1}}

| Term | Content | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| acquirer | Individual or organization acquiring the system | Zoo owner who will buy an elephant in 3 years |
| system | Implementations such as applications, subsystems, collections of systems, product lines, product families | Elephant |
| mission | Intended use/operation method of the system by one or more stakeholders within the environment | Raising an elephant that weighs 1.5 tons, has large ears, and can run 7 km/h |
| environment | Factors influencing the system, such as development, operation, political external factors | 3-year project period, enclosure for the elephant to grow, seasons, market price of elephants |
| stakeholder | One or more interested parties in the system, each with different concerns about the system, individuals or organizations | Trainer, zoo owner |
| concerns | Aspects of system development or operation important to one or more stakeholders, including system performance, flexibility, security, distribution, evolution | Trainer's concern is how to grow the elephant healthily to 1.5 tons. Zoo owner's concern is how much zoo revenue can be increased by buying this elephant. |
| architectural description | Recommended method of execution to suit the environment during system construction, how architecture is documented | Elephant training log |
| view | - A perspective on a set of concerns for the entire system - An architectural description consists of multiple views - A method of representing the system's architecture according to a specific viewpoint - Composed of one or more architectural models | The trainer's idea of how the elephant grows is the 1st view (dynamic), the trainer's idea of a magnificent elephant is the 2nd view (static). The zoo owner's idea of a 1.5-ton elephant with large ears that runs 7 km/h is the 3rd view (static). |
| viewpoint | A perspective that establishes criteria for how a view is created, described, or analyzed, determining what language (notation, model, product types) will be used to express the view - A pattern or template for expressing concerns | The trainer's method of expressing an ideal elephant |

 b. UML 4+1 View
 

| Perspective | Description (UML Diagram) |
| --- | --- |
| Use Case View | User's perspective of actual use (Use-Case) |
| Design View | System's structure and function perspective to provide required features (Collaboration, Class) |
| Process View | System's behavior perspective (Activity) |
| Implementation View | Perspective of implementing the system's software and hardware (Component) |
| Deployment View | Perspective of the physical deployment composing the system (Deployment) |

 
 c. SAD (Software Architecture Document)
  - SAD Utilization Methods: 
   Educational, communication tool, input for system evaluation and analysis process
  - 7 Guidelines for SAD Creation
      1) Write the document from the reader's perspective
      2) Eliminate unnecessary repetition
      3) Avoid ambiguity
      4) Adhere to standard structure
      5) Document rationale
      6) Keep the document up-to-date
      7) Review afterward to ensure it meets its purpose
  {{IMG:2}}

** d. 7 Roles of an Architect (Defined in Applied Software Architecture)**

1. Presenting the project's vision
2. Consultant capable of advising on core technologies
3. Decision-maker for critical issues faced by the project
4. Coaching role for architecture
5. Mediator resolving conflicts
6. Software implementation engineer
7. Advocate for the importance of architecture

**4. Architecture Evaluation Models**
 {{IMG:3}}

| | ATAM | ° An architecture evaluation method that not only judges whether the architecture satisfies quality attributes but also analyzes how they conflict (tradeoff) and interact. ° Evaluates all Quality Attributes. ° Focuses on finding Sensitivity points and Tradeoff points. |
| --- | --- |
| SAAM | ° The first formalized architecture evaluation method. ° A method for evaluating and analyzing architecture from various modifiability perspectives. ° Less detailed than ATAM, but can be applied to a wider range of areas. |
| CBAM | ° Evaluates software architecture from an ROI perspective. ° Considers the economic aspects of the benefits derived from the quality provided by the system. ° Selects the software architecture that maximizes profit by calculating ROI based on costs and benefits. |

titleEn: [Software Engineering] Development Methodologies
contentEn:
Topic: Development Methodology
Author: Forest Story ([http://blog.naver.com/fstory97](http://blog.naver.com/fstory97))
Date: May 19, 2009
Related URL: [http://blog.naver.com/inter999/140050301281](http://blog.naver.com/inter999/140050301281)
[http://blog.naver.com/inter999/140050306389](http://blog.naver.com/inter999/140050306389)
[http://blog.naver.com/inter999/140050576771](http://blog.naver.com/inter999/140050576771)
[http://blog.naver.com/inter999/140060864396](http://blog.naver.com/inter999/140060864396)
[http://cafe.naver.com/sojw/3465](http://cafe.naver.com/sojw/3465)

**1. Related Topics from Past Exam Questions**
- CBD
- RUP
- SW Architecture
- Package
- Component Interface
**2. Role of Development Methodology**
- Repetitive pattern for solving problems
- Standardization: Easy understanding among stakeholders
- Structuring: Structures problems for easier understanding and solution
- Improved reusability: Contributes to increasing the reusability of deliverables
**3. Components of Development Methodology**
- Stages: Development methodology approaches the development process by dividing it into chronological stages.
- Time: Cost incurred for performing the development methodology.
- Activities: Specifies activities for each stage.
- Deliverables: Necessary deliverables for each activity.
- Development Techniques: Design perspective aimed for during development.
- Stakeholders (Organization): Entities performing the development methodology.
**4. Types and Evolution of Development Methodologies: Evolved towards increasing reusability**
- **Structured Development Methodology (Process-Oriented Methodology)**
: Period: 1970s
: Perspective: Function-centric
: Based on the SDLC Waterfall Model
: Principle of Divide and Conquer
: Low reusability
- **Information Engineering Methodology (Data-Oriented Methodology)**
: Period: 1980s
: Perspective: Data-centric
: Useful for database modeling
: Functional elements not considered
- **Object-Oriented Methodology (Object-Oriented Methodology)**
: Period: 1990s
: Perspective: Object-centric
: Functions (Behavior) and data (Attribute) are embedded in objects.
: Encapsulation, Abstraction, Inheritance, Polymorphism
: Increased reusability but difficult to implement (mainly a concept during implementation)
: Dependent on development language
- **Component-Based Methodology (Component-Based Methodology)**
: Period: 2000s
: Perspective: Component-centric
: Emphasizes black-box interfaces (runtime) objects
: OOP and CBD are mutually cooperative, each component can be developed with OOP.
: Objects called by remote procedures are sometimes collectively referred to as components.
: Independent of development language
- **Aspect-Oriented Methodology (Aspect-Oriented Methodology)**
: Period: After 2000
: Perspective: Core concerns (business logic) and cross-cutting concerns (logging, security, transactions, etc., commonly applied)
: Emerged due to the difficulty of implementing distributed and intertwined OOP in complex systems.
: Separates cross-cutting concerns (Advice) and core concerns (Code) to build a system through a Weaving process that creates Point-cuts.
- **Agile Methodology**
: Features:
-> Direct feedback activities with customers
-> Short phases, not hesitant to change
-> Not dependent on deliverables
-> Includes human activities that may occur during the development process, not just specific stages.
: Types
l XP
- Suitable for small-scale development, emphasizes customer feedback
- Key activities: Code Review, TDD, Pair Programming, etc.
l UP
- Suitable for large-scale projects
- Stage-specific activities are not explicit, but key processes exist.
- Replaced by RUP, a cohesive and well-crafted web-based documentation set from Rational Software, describing the Rational Unified Process.
l SCRUM
- When issues are cleared, they are removed from SCRUM.
- Weekly check-ins
- High visibility
l SPRINT
- Short SPRINTs of one month
- Meetings are weekly, within 15 minutes.
- **Service-Oriented Methodology (Service-Oriented Methodology)**
: Period: After 2000
: Perspective: Service-centric
: Service-unit design for reusability from a business user perspective.
: Web-based, considering compatibility between heterogeneous systems.
: SOA

**5. Comparison of Architecture, Framework, and Development Methodology**
- Architecture: The structure of an actual, materialized system.
- Framework: Semi-finished software; programs are implemented based on the framework.
- A framework is semi-finished software built upon methodologies and architecture.
- Development Methodology: A formalized set of activities for implementing software.

**6. Function, Class, Object, Package, Component, Interface, Service**
- Function: The smallest functional unit with input/output possible during software implementation.
- Class: A specification for an object, consisting of data Attributes and function Behaviors, a concept for modeling real-world objects.
- Object: A materialized concept of a class, a class at runtime.
- Package: A collection of classes, a set of classes from a user's perspective, also indicating belonging.
- Component: A runtime object with an interface, a language-independent procedure.
- Interface: A function contract for calling the functionality of a component.
- Service: A functional unit from a business user's perspective.

**7. Issues in Applying Development Methodologies**
- Exclusion of formal documentation: Education, CMMi adoption
- Avoid blind faith in methodologies
- Selection of appropriate methodology
- Understanding the characteristics of each methodology and current business domain
- Customization of methodologies
- Multiple methodologies can be used appropriately and simultaneously.
: Examples of complementary methodologies
- Services are implemented with Components.
- Components are implemented with Classes.
- The scope of Class implementation can be selected using AOP.
- Database modeling uses information engineering methodology.
- Class Method implementation uses structured methodology.
- Development activities use XP with TDD, Pair Programming, and Code Review.

titleEn: A Webtoon in Memory of the Late President Roh Moo-hyun
contentEn:
Cartoonists from all portals drew memorial webtoons for former President Roh Moo-hyun, each with a message.
Even competing portals are all sharing and posting each other's content.
[http://comic.naver.com/webtoon/list.nhn?titleId=69113&menuType=&weekday=wed](http://comic.naver.com/webtoon/list.nhn?titleId=69113&menuType=&weekday=wed)
It's truly a wonderful thing.

But when I look at those comics, there's so much content that truly overwhelms me with emotion.

Could there be words more poignant than these?
Many people scoffed, saying the internet was Roh Moo-hyun's space.
True. Information on the internet is biased.
But it also possesses collective intelligence.

That's why many efforts are made to distort that collective intelligence.
However, within that collective intelligence, hubs exist. These webtoons are a prime example.
Drawing comics requires more effort and labor than writing. Therefore, these hubs generally know the truth very well, and every single scene is precious to them. This is because as high-quality content producers, they must confront many truths and engage in much thought.

It's different from the cheap comments on Naver News, which are dominated by certain online communities.
I, too, tried not to write emotional posts on my blog as much as possible.
Although it was a service of a company I used to work for, I don't look at the Naver News comment section these days.
That comment section is just a cheap anonymous bulletin board that has lost its value as information.

I've always liked cartoonists, but I was surprised that they, too, were thinking this deeply.
I, too, had actually remained silent. In the past, when I was called a "Roh-ppa" (Roh fanboy/fangirl), I liked Roh Moo-hyun, but I disliked the term "ppa" and didn't show it much. And perhaps because I disliked such terms, I tried my best to logically find more good things he had done that would make him likable.

Former President Roh Moo-hyun reduced the information gap, so now even older people are coming online. Is it thanks to that? That people with old-fashioned ideas, like those behind "No-No Demo," have occupied a part of the internet and turned it into an emotional garbage dump...

I actually resent former President Roh Moo-hyun.
He should have fought until the end. Thanks to that, it feels like we, the incompetent ones, have been stripped bare.
The truly shameful ones are not the greedy people scrambling to fill their own pockets, but rather us, who thought too lightly of casting a vote, swallowed our opinions, and only secretly admired people like Roh Moo-hyun.

He left too many tasks when he died. He's a hateful person.
There's still a long time until the election... I'm worried because both I and the Korean people are like "nambi" (hot-tempered and quick to forget).

titleEn: [Terminator 4] The Return of
contentEn:
{{IMG:1}}

http://movie.naver.com/movie/bi/mi/review.nhn?code=66520

			
				

#### [Terminator Salvation](http://movie.naver.com/movie/bi/mi/review.nhn?code=66520)

				Director McG
				Cast Christian Bale, Sam Worthington, Anton Yelchin, Moon Bloodgood
				Production 2009 USA, Germany, UK, 115 minutes
				**Rating**

**1. Terminator 4, an Homage to Terminator 1 & 2**
I watched the much-anticipated Terminator 4. It was at least better than the 3rd installment, and slightly below the 2nd. Still, if you're a fan of the sci-fi genre, I recommend watching it. Compared to the 3rd film, where Arnold Schwarzenegger looked visibly struggling, the 4th film feels much more like a return to form for Terminator.
Was it because John Connor was in his rebellious phase? In fact, the 3rd film didn't really advance from the 2nd.
The stale theme of the boundary between humans and robots was bland, and it failed to show the overwhelming presence of the Terminator. Actually, the boundary between humans and robots was so perfectly resolved in the 2nd film that even in the 4th, concretized by Marcus, it didn't feel new. The only things the 3rd film showed were the fact that Skynet was a highly resilient distributed computer and the confirmation that humanity's future couldn't be changed.
The 4th film can be considered an homage to the 1st and 2nd films. Many visual scenes directly borrowed from the 1st, and we could also appreciate the muscular physique of Governor Arnold from his younger days.

{{IMG:2}}

**2. The Terminator's Time Paradox Begins Anew (Even More Complex!)**
Since the boundary between robots and humans was essentially resolved in the 2nd film, there's nothing more to say about it. Let's interpret this movie by focusing on the core fun of Terminator: time travel.
Some people, when discussing Terminator's time theory, say that the 1st film was about fatalism, where time travel is just one paradigm of fate.
However, the 2nd film introduced the idea of parallel universes, where humanity's future is determined by humans as pioneers. But the 3rd film again leaned towards fatalism.
So, what about the 4th film? Up until now, the Terminator series has had its story advanced by different directors and different people.
But if we forcibly connect them, we inevitably return to the situation of the 1st film. In the 4th film, John Connor mutters, "This is different from the future I know." And why did he think that? It's because of the information passed to him through Kyle and his mother, which was data given to him by his future self. What can explain the Terminator's worldview are precisely those things that came from the future.
From the data to win the war against the Terminators, he learned many things, and perhaps even information about future machines Skynet would develop. But let's go further into the future. At the point when John Connor was winning the war, Skynet and John Connor dispatched people to the past. In other words, he clearly knew all the tactics, strategies, and enemy weaknesses to conquer Skynet.
But why didn't the wise leader John Connor convey such crucial strategic information to his past self? Or why didn't he tell him the plan to destroy Skynet from the beginning?
Perhaps, if we consider that the scenarios of 2, 3, and 4 were facts already experienced by future John Connor, everything makes sense. It means he already knew the information that needed to be sent to the past. And as the winner of a game he was already winning, there was no real reason to change the past. There was only the human reason, as Sarah Connor said, of having to make the painful decision to send his own father to the past, knowing he would die.
In fact, throughout 1, 2, 3, and 4, many people died in the fight against Terminators from the future. Even John Connor's adoptive parents. In the 4th film, even the strategic submarine of the global military is sunk. And John Connor actually becomes the leader of the resistance. If they had lived, could John Connor have become the resistance leader?

**3. John Connor's Conspiracy**
So, now it's clear. Future John Connor knew about Marcus, and that the frequency was fake. Because he had already experienced it. We assumed the 2nd film implied a parallel universe, but it was only believed to be so due to the concealment of information from the future; it wasn't actually true. John Connor deliberately didn't create a link to transmit information to his past self. The reason is that if he had transmitted that information, he wouldn't have been confident that he could truly become the leader of the resistance and create the present where Skynet is defeated. He must have thought that pulling out one foundational stone could collapse the present he had painstakingly built. In other words, fearing the destruction of his own existence, future John Connor sent limited information from the future to the past, based on what he had already experienced. And, in fact, this didn't just lead to Kyle's death. It means all those who died in 1, 2, 3, and 4 were also his responsibility.
{{IMG:3}}

**4. Skynet, John Connor's Twin**
Now, let's turn to Skynet. What on earth was future Skynet thinking when it sent Terminators to the past? In fact, Skynet's actions weren't entirely logical. There's only one possible explanation: the information from the future sent to the past was not acquired by the present Skynet. If I were Skynet, I would have created a link to transmit as much current information as possible to the past Skynet. If the submarine hadn't been captured, humanity would have been embroiled in internal strife, and Marcus might not have been created. Clearly, Skynet, whether by future John Connor or for some other reason, seems to have failed to send information from the future to the past.
Also, there's a fact Skynet must avoid: it must not interfere with its own birth. Skynet, like John Connor who was born from Kyle who came from the future, is a twin born from Terminator technology that came from the future. Here, a time paradox arises. In fact, if John Connor were killed at the wrong time, Skynet might not have been developed either.
Reaching this point in my thoughts, one thing becomes clear: Skynet's objective is to eliminate John Connor while minimizing interference with its own birth. Perhaps that part was too complex for Skynet to make the right decision. And, just like John Connor, Skynet also faces the problem of not being able to send all information to the past.

**5. Parallel Universes Never Existed! In Fact, It Was All Predetermined.**
Thinking this far, it becomes clear. The entire story was already set. Marcus was not a variable but a planned event that was bound to happen. He was an indispensable medium for delivering the heart to John Connor, making John Connor the leader of humanity, and sending Kyle to the past. Therefore, just as information was concealed from Kyle, future John Connor also did not tell his past self about Marcus.
Future Skynet might have realized this fact as well. That this fight was futile. But, if it didn't send Terminators to the past, it too could not exist. It becomes clear that Terminator is not about parallel theories. In the first film, Kyle's flashback shows a scar on John Connor's face, which is created in this film. Ultimately, the 4th film makes the story fit together perfectly.
This kind of worldview actually already exists. It's the Bible. The New and Old Testaments are structured in such a way. Prophecy and the fulfillment of prophecy. Those who try to change the prophecy. But even that becomes part of fulfilling the prophecy. Watching Terminator, I felt it was similar to that.

**6. Terminator 5?**
So, how will John Connor defeat Skynet in the future? I think there are some subtle hints in the movie.
Marcus directly connected to Skynet and downloaded a lot of data in an instant. What could that content be? Did the information he possessed truly die with him? John Connor's wife was shown to be pregnant. Also, the black girl named Star who accompanied Connor. Was she there just to make it less awkward for John Connor to be alone? The next scenario is likely to involve those children. In the next installment, will T800 Arnold be mass-produced???
{{IMG:4}}
Of course, the framework I've thought up could all collapse depending on how Terminator 5 is made. ^^; It's good that movies are fun to interpret.

**6. Perhaps Predetermined, Yet Meaningful Present**
The future might be predetermined. And in fact, from a scientific perspective, it is predetermined. Human knowledge is just a type of chemical reaction, and it was all set from the time of the Big Bang. However, the reason humanity constantly thinks and John Connor tirelessly fights is because without doing so, there would be no valuable future to gain. Isn't that the worldview of Terminator?

**ps. How to Defeat Skynet from a Technical Standpoint**
If Skynet was a system that enhanced its survivability through distributed computing, seeing Skynet now misleading humans with false information reminds me of the security term 'honeypot'. You intentionally create vulnerabilities in a system, monitor hacker attack patterns, and then use that information to respond when the real core is attacked. Skynet intentionally created vulnerabilities, threw out bait, and when humans attacked, it updated its system. It's precisely a defensive technique using a honeypot.
So, what's the best way to destroy distributed computing? The best method is, again, a distributed attack. Skynet is an aggregate of wired and wireless networks. Regarding power, it already uses nuclear and smart grid technology, so paralyzing the power system would be difficult. The network itself must be paralyzed or taken over. If that's not possible, since Skynet is also software, the best option would be to somehow hack and patch the corresponding program.
Fighting and defeating Skynet with an updated, variant Skynet. This seems to be the best approach.

titleEn: Why the World is Less Interested in Korea Than
contentEn:
** **[**http://limwonki.com/263**](http://limwonki.com/263)** My Opinion on [Is Korea an Internet Island Nation?](http://limwonki.com/263)**
**** 
I don't think the reason is that Korea's information is an island.

In Japan, Google's market share is extremely low, and they use SNS platforms that are only popular in Japan. Also, due to the Japanese personality, they don't particularly enjoy socializing with strangers. Looking at the market itself, Japan is as much an information island nation as Korea.
Even if Korea suddenly changed its national language to English, or if Google became the number one search engine in Korea, the situation wouldn't change. It doesn't seem to have much to do with openness. Rather, it's a problem with the quality of Korean content. Google has taken over the internet in almost every country worldwide, with the exception of about six nations. However, not all of those countries become subjects of discussion.
Since Korea lacks leading industries, foreigners have little to search for beyond community-related content. Japan, on the other hand, has more core technologies than we realize. It's a nation that launches rockets independently and lands spacecraft on asteroids. Even in the mobile phone and semiconductor industries, where Korea is said to be number one, most core technologies are foreign. At best, there was CDMA... and more recently, Wibro.
There's one reason why Koreans specifically search for English materials on Google: there's no domestic data, and the technology isn't domestic. Even if Korea is dependent on MS technology, the reality is that to find MS technical documents, you have to Google and search in English-speaking regions. This is because MS is an American company, and they create and release information first in the US. Even famous domestic bloggers are busy translating and reposting articles from famous overseas bloggers, and skilled engineers search foreign English sites, not Korean sites via Google. When it comes to Korean search, Google and Naver are much of a muchness. From the outset, useful Korean content is often hidden away on paid sites. Furthermore, without original Korean content, there's no interest from abroad. Virtualization blogs, SNS, and cloud computing are all technologies that originated overseas.
It would be better to hope that Naver or Cyworld would promote themselves successfully overseas, rather than expecting Korean internet to gain influence.
Think about it from an international perspective. Is there any reason to go through the trouble of learning difficult Korean to view Korean websites? Beyond information for Korean expatriates and Hallyu (Korean Wave) content, there isn't. In Japan's case, such reasons clearly exist. This applies to academic information, as well as cultural content like animation and books. Why would anyone come to Korea to search for IT data? MS, Google, Oracle, IBM, Apple, HP are all American companies. And when it comes to cultural content, Japan is overwhelmingly dominant. Its population is about 2-3 times that of Korea, but its production and consumption of cultural content are far greater. (Among these, there's quite a bit of adult material...--; it's fair to say that half of the internet is adult material, and its impact is surprisingly huge.) It's often the case that search results for Samsung Electronics' new products are better or faster from overseas sources. No matter how much Tistory or blogs discuss Korean socio-economic issues, overseas audiences won't pay attention. It would be better to create and sell something like D-War instead.

This is also why things like 'Knowledge-in' (Naver's Q&A), Tistory, or the 'Candlelight Vigils' are ultimately just storms in a teacup.
What overseas refers to as an 'IT powerhouse' is about network games and internet infrastructure, not internet content. If we compare the quantity and quality of information with English-speaking regions, we might just be emerging from the PC communication era.

It seems the government is making a lot of such blunders these days. To attract tourists, a region needs unique attractions. If each region competitively paves roads well and boasts about imitating or improving upon cool things from other regions, people won't come. Even near Seoul, there are many great things along the Han River, so who would travel all the way to the Nakdong River just to see water?

From an international perspective, the reason for a lack of interest in Korea is that the level of information or reward received is low compared to the cost of the language barrier one must overcome to access the Korean internet.

titleEn: [Idea] Video Conferencing with Audio Processing Based
contentEn:
1. Title: Voice Processing for Video Conferencing Based on Speaker Distance
2. Background: During video conferences, two types of information are transmitted: audio and video. However, audio only directly transmits information from the microphone, with no linkage to the video. We considered an implementation method based on the idea that varying the audio volume according to the speaker's distance from the camera could enhance the sense of presence.
3. Implementation Sections
    1) Audio/Video Input Unit – A common component used in typical video conferences.
    2) Distance Measurement Unit – Measures how far the speaker is from the camera. This could involve video processing using a camera, or it could be a stereo camera or various other devices.
    3) Audio Processing Unit – Refers to the section that applies post-processing, such as audio volume or effects, based on the measured distance. (This audio processing unit can reside on the server hosting the conference or on the client.)
    4) Network – The processed audio is transmitted via the network.
    5) Audio Output Unit – The part where audio is output by mixing the voices of 'n' speakers. Typically a speaker.
4. Details of the Audio Processing Unit
    *   When data is received from the distance measurement unit indicating that speakers A, B, and C are at distances of 1, 1.5, and 2 respectively, the audio processing unit divides the frequency of speakers A, B, and C's voices by 1, 1.5, and 2 respectively, to determine their relative volumes.

titleEn: [Idea] Open Marketplace Using NPCs in Online Games
contentEn:
1. Open Market using NPCs within Online Games
 Current: In most games, a market is opened to create a marketplace for item trading and sales.
 
2. Improvements
 - Like current open markets, sellers propose items and prices they wish to sell to the [Open Market Broker NPC].
  Items are transferred to the broker, and unsold items can be retrieved by the seller.
 
 - Buyers can check the lowest price and quantity of items they wish to purchase from the [Open Market Broker NPC].
 - Buyers can check the average transaction price and the lowest transaction price of items they wish to purchase.
 
 - The open market utilizes information only from regional open markets, not global open market information within the game.
   (Therefore, transaction prices may vary by region, which can serve as a function to stimulate economic activity.)
 
 - If there are no items or quantities at the desired price, buyers can propose a price and item to the [Open Market Broker NPC].
  Similarly, money is transferred to the broker, and unspent money can be retrieved by the buyer.
 
 - Once a sale/purchase transaction is completed, the item or money is transferred to the seller/buyer.
   The seller who sold the item can retrieve the money from the [Open Market Broker NPC],
   and the buyer who intended to purchase the item can retrieve the item from the [Open Market Broker NPC].
 
 - During sales/purchase activities, the NPC may take a small commission, and commissions may vary by open market within the same game.
   (Also includes an economic element)
 
 - Buyers who purchased an item may also return it within a specified period.
   (Returns may not be accepted if the item has been used or damaged.)
   If such a system is applied, it can protect buyers, and during the specified period, the NPC does not pay the sales proceeds to the seller, informing the seller that it is a return period.
 
3. Differentiators
 - While existing online commerce involves immediate purchase activity,
   this system involves entrusting the NPC, and the NPC acts as a broker.
 (There is a patent for entrusted purchases below, but purchase activity still occurs immediately.
There doesn't seem to be a system where one visits an NPC to retrieve sold proceeds or purchased items.)
 
- Actual NPC open market economic activity occurs by region within the game.
 (While economic activity by region exists in games like 'Uncharted Waters',
it does not occur in user markets,
 and the information available to buyers is very limited.)
